title: 第六章 世俗共和国与神权式“帝国理念”
originalTitle: 6 The Secular Republic and the Theocratic “Imperial Idea”

zh: 本书迄今呈现了一个关于拜占庭政治之意识形态与实践的模型，它略去了学者们惯常所称的“帝国理念”，即皇帝由基督教上帝任命来统治的理论。这一理念的确切表述在史料与现代学术中各有不同，不过与其同我所呈现模型之间那道巨大鸿沟相比，其变异幅度很小。这里牵涉的是两种实质上不同的看待皇权的方式。帝国理念引出若干主张。皇帝有权或有义务贯彻上帝的意志，臣民把他视为宗教人物而对他心怀敬畏，他与臣民的交往也由宗教来界定。这一理念的种种版本几乎见于所有关于拜占庭的学术著作。对它的复述是公式化而重复的。有一条不成文的规矩：学者必须先向它致敬，然后才能转入其书文的具体题目。它被当作一个阿基米德点，一个固定的中心，拜占庭世界围绕它旋转，而我们可借它撬动其从属的方方面面。它被赋予如此的分量与权威，以致相比之下该文化的罗马面向显得像是只值得古物研究者留意的遗存，而且常被如此称呼。事实上，所谓拜占庭皇帝的神授之权被赋予如此分量，以致有些学者仅凭它一点就把“罗马”时期与“拜占庭”时期区分开来。
en: This study has so far presented a model for the ideology and practice of politics in Byzantium that omits what scholars conventionally call the “imperial idea,” namely, the theory that the emperor was appointed to rule by the Christian God. The exact formulation of this idea varies in the sources and modern scholarship, though the range of variation is small compared to the vast gulf that separates it from the model that I have presented. At issue are two substantially different ways of perceiving imperial power. Various consequences flowed out from the imperial idea, including that the emperor was authorized, or required, to carry out God’s will; that he was viewed by subjects with awe as a religious figure; and that his dealings with his subjects were defined religiously. Versions of this idea are found in almost all the scholarship on Byzantium. Its recitation is formulaic and repetitive. There is an unwritten rule that scholars must offer it homage before moving on to the particular topic of their books and articles. It is treated as an Archimedean point, a fixed center around which the Byzantine world revolved and from which we can leverage its subordinate aspects. It is given such weight and authority that the Roman aspects of the culture seem like quaint antiquarian survivals by comparison, and are often called that. In fact, the alleged divine right of the Byzantine emperors is given such weight that some scholars separate the “Roman” and the “Byzantine” periods based on it alone.

zh: 本章将把那幅图景整个颠倒过来。引人注目的是，几乎没有什么晚近学术致力于对帝国理念本身、其史料、社会语境与历史意涵作批判性考察。在拜占庭学中确立它的那些著作既陈旧又有问题。于是，未经审视，帝国理念已成了一条教义，被当作不证自明的真理被反复套用。它伴随着对拜占庭人罗马身份的隐含（虽有时是明确）否认，以及一种持续的失败——未能认识到他们生活在一个只能被称为共和国的政体之中。
en: This chapter will turn that picture on its head. It is striking that there is almost no recent scholarship devoted to a critical examination of the imperial idea itself, its sources, social context, and historical implications. The works that established it in Byzantine Studies are dated and problematic. So without having been scrutinized, the imperial idea has become a doctrine, recycled endlessly as a self-evident truth. It accompanies the implicit (though sometimes explicit) denial of the Byzantines’ Roman identity and the persistent failure to realize that they lived in what can only be called a republic.

zh: “帝国理念”的轮廓与限度
en: The Contours and Limits of the “Imperial Idea”

zh: 对帝国理念的仪式性诵念是做一名拜占庭学家的一部分，所以我无意在此特意挑出我将引用的那些学者，他们的名字我通常不会在正文中提及。同样的公式可以从数以百计、用各种学术语言写成的出版物中引到。不过，我要提请读者注意保罗·亚历山大（Paul Alexander）1962年那篇有影响力的文章，它比其余诸篇被引用得更多，并作为“经典”重印过。在我看来这篇文章是一部错误大全，但我们稍后再谈这一点。
en: Ritual incantation of the imperial idea is part of being a Byzantinist, so I do not mean to single out the scholars I will be citing here, whose names I will normally not mention in the text. The same formula can be cited from hundreds of publications in every language of scholarship. I will, however, draw attention to an influential article from 1962 by Paul Alexander, which is cited more than the rest and is reprinted as a “classic.” In my view this article is a Compendium of Errors, but we will get to that later.

zh: 在拜占庭人看来，皇帝作为上帝在世间的形象与代表，是他们整个基督教世界唯一正当的统治者。作为上帝的总督，他受命维护基督教世界的和平、承担向“蛮族”传教的基督教使命、并保全法律……皇帝由上帝拣选，而且如上文所见，到了末世，末代拜占庭皇帝将促成从地上王国向天上王国的过渡。
en: In the Byzantine view the emperor was the only legitimate ruler of their entire Christian world in his capacity as God’s image and representative on earth. As God’s viceroy he was charged with the maintenance of peace in the Christian world, with the Christian mission to the “barbarians,” and with the preservation of law... The emperor was selected by God and, as was seen above, at the end of time the last Byzantine emperor would bring about the transition from the earthly to the heavenly kingdom.

zh: 按照当前拜占庭学的范式，这就是拜占庭人看待其皇帝的方式。“神权政体”一词在这个领域里被大量抛出，“绝对主义”之类亦然（如今的争论是该用“神权的”还是“以上帝为中心的”）。
当拜占庭皇帝在大多数书文中被引入和界定时，首先是、而且往往唯一地是相对于上帝，而非相对于他所治理的
。在许多研究中，
根本缺席——不仅作为一个重要概念缺席，更作为拜占庭政治存在论的一个关键要素缺席。于是，当我们把这套“理念”（其要素取自一组特定文本，大多是颂辞，外加几部启示录式的幻想）摆在我在前几章呈现的拜占庭政治模型旁边时，我们遇到了一道几乎无法跨越的鸿沟。罗马的君主制共和国不可能等同于东正教的帝国神权政体。两者不可能指同一个社会——然而它们指的却是同一个。我将在本章试图弥合的正是这道鸿沟。
en: That, according to the current paradigm of Byzantine Studies, is how the Byzantines viewed their emperor. The word “theocracy” is thrown around a lot in the field as is “absolutism” and the like (the debate now is whether to use “theocratic” or “theocentric”).
When the Byzantine emperor is introduced and defined in most books and articles it is first, and often exclusively, in relation to God, not the
that he governed. In many studies the

is altogether absent, not just as an important concept but as a crucial element of Byzantine political ontology. So when we set the “idea,” whose elements are drawn from a particular set of texts (mostly panegyrical and a few apocalyptic fantasies), next to the model of Byzantine politics that I presented in the previous chapters, we encounter an almost unbridgeable gap. The Roman monarchical republic cannot have been the same as the Orthodox imperial theocracy. The two cannot be referring to the same society—and yet they are. It is this gap that I will try to close in the present chapter.

zh: 首先必须就帝国理念在现代学术中的历史说几句。第一，那些表面上确立它的研究已经过时、如今大有问题，却仍被当作权威引用。例如，我们上文看到，一部2005年出版的关于罗马帝国衰亡的研究声称，在拜占庭“一切共和主义的伪装都已消失……没有人把皇帝看作专制君主以外的任何东西……正当的统治者皆受神启、由神拣选。”
为支撑此说而引用的著作是弗朗西斯·德沃尔尼克神父（Fr. Francis Dvornik）的《早期基督教与拜占庭政治哲学：起源与背景》（

children: Early Christian and Byzantine Political Philosophy: Origins and Background

zh: ，1966）。关于德沃尔尼克这部庞大综述，除了其宗教倾向之外，值得指出的一点是：它设有论埃及、美索不达米亚、赫梯人与《旧约》的章节，却对罗马政治思想与实践只字不提，仿佛那些与拜占庭研究无关。德沃尔尼克在另一部书（2008）中被引为证据，以支撑“晚期罗马帝国的意识形态已彻底基督教化”这一断言。
2011年的又一部书就拜占庭政治意识形态引用了德沃尔尼克、亚历山大，以及贝恩斯（Baynes）1933年论优西比乌的文章。
en: A few remarks must first be made about the history of the imperial idea in modern scholarship. First, the studies that ostensibly established it are outdated and now problematic, but they are still cited as authoritative. For example, we saw above that a study of the fall of the Roman empire, published in 2005, claims that in Byzantium “all pretense of republicanism had vanished... no one thought of the emperor as anything other than an autocratic monarch... legitimate rulers were divinely inspired and divinely chosen.”
The work cited in support of this is Fr. Francis Dvornik’s

children: Early Christian and Byzantine Political Philosophy: Origins and Background

en: (1966). A point worth making about Dvornik’s massive survey, apart from its religious slant, is that it has chapters on Egypt, Mesopotamia, the Hittites, and the Old Testament, but nothing on Roman political thought and practice, as if those were irrelevant to the study of Byzantium. Dvornik is cited in another book (2008) as proof of the claim that “the ideology of the late Roman empire had become thoroughly Christian.”
Another book from 2011 cites for Byzantine political ideology Dvornik, Alexander, and Baynes’s 1933 article on Eusebios.

zh: 优西比乌（Eusebios）是巴勒斯坦凯撒利亚的主教，亲历了戴克里先的大迫害与君士坦丁皈依基督教。据现存文献，他是第一位试图解释这些事件、并从基督教立场思考出现一位基督徒皇帝意味着什么的基督教作家。他制定出大致如上所述的帝国理念，并用它来赞美君士坦丁。结果，他在这个领域里被当作某种“拜占庭宪法”的作者来对待。几乎每一个想要说明拜占庭人如何看待政治或皇帝的学者，都会搬出几段优西比乌的引文。
en: Eusebios was the bishop of Kaisareia in Palestine who lived through the Great Persecution of Diocletian and Constantine’s conversion to Christianity. He was the first Christian writer we have who tried to make sense of those events and explain in Christian terms what it might mean to have a Christian emperor. He worked out something like the imperial idea outlined above and used it to praise Constantine. As a result, he is treated in the field as if he were the author of a kind of “Byzantine Constitution.” Almost every scholar who wants to illustrate what the Byzantines thought about politics or the emperor trots out some quotations from Eusebios.

zh: 如果说拜占庭国家有一套官方政治理论作为基础，那就是凯撒利亚的优西比乌为君士坦丁大帝构想的基督教皇权理论；按照该理论，帝国是天国的缩影，皇帝由上帝安置于此，以确保正信得以延续。
en: Insofar as there was an official political theory underpinning the Byzantine state, it consisted of the Christianized-ruler theory worked out for Constantine the Great by Eusebius of Caesarea, according to which the empire was the microcosm of heaven and the emperor placed there by God to ensure the maintenance of true religion.

zh: 紧接着下一页又引了另一位历史学家的话：“拜占庭被恰当地描述为一个神权政体。”
en: This is followed on the next page by a quotation from another historian that “Byzantium is rightly described as a theocracy.”

zh: 除其他目标外，本章还将把优西比乌放回他恰当的位置，办法是借助比1933年更晚近的、关于他及其语境的研究。眼下我继续勾勒“帝国理念”的轮廓。第三点是，它的吸引力很大程度上在于它提供了把文本与图像研究结合起来的机会。皇帝在拜占庭艺术的许多媒介中被表现，而反映帝国理念诸版本的文本提供了一把诱人的钥匙，可用以开启它们的意义。于是艺术史家得以使用文本，反过来，历史学家也得以通过复制视觉插图来配合其文本，从而营造出文化深度的印象。此处的奠基性研究追溯到1936年，至今仍被当作权威引用。
此外，文本与艺术又能反过来被嵌入宫廷仪式的语境，后者提供了帝国理念的一幅活生生图像。要记住这些材料大多由宫廷产生，当它们被汇集起来时，便呈现出一幅看似统一的文化图景——这正是那些挣扎着要把思想（神话）与仪式综合起来的历史学家难以企及的目标。
在拜占庭，它们为我们无缝而毫不费力地汇合在一起。此处阿尔弗尔迪（Alföldi）与特赖廷格（Treitinger）的奠基性研究同样追溯到1930年代。
en: Among its other aims, this chapter will put Eusebios in his proper place, by drawing on studies of him and his context that are more recent than 1933. For now I will continue sketching the contours of the “imperial idea.” A third point is that much of its appeal lies in the opportunity it presents to combine the study of texts and images. Emperors were represented in many media of Byzantine art, and texts that reflect versions of the imperial idea offer a tempting key by which to unlock their meaning. So art historians get to use texts and, conversely, historians get to create the impression of cultural depth by reproducing visual illustrations to accompany their texts. The foundational study here dates to 1936, and is cited as authoritative still.

Moreover, the texts and the art can in turn be embedded in the context of court ceremonies, which provide a living image of the imperial idea. Keeping in mind that most of this material was generated by the court, when assembled it presents what appears to be a unified picture of the culture, the elusive goal of historians who struggle to synthesize thought (myth) and ritual.
In Byzantium they come together for us seamlessly and effortlessly. The foundational studies here by Alföldi and Treitinger again date to the 1930s.

zh: 简言之，如果我们想理解自己为何对拜占庭皇帝持有如今这些看法，就需要先理解1930年代学者们正在努力应对的那些政治议题，以及拜占庭如何被卷入其中。说得客气些，就思考绝对权力而言，1930年代不是一个寻常的十年。然而我不打算展开这样一种分析。我在此的焦点将是拜占庭。我将提供一种理解“帝国理念”的替代方式，它将揭示这个领域的先驱们选择抬高什么、略去什么，以及他们认为什么才算政治意识形态。例如，1930年代的学者被神权观念所吸引，却不知如何将其语境化。他们也不认为宫廷之外任何人的实际行为与决定是相关的。这正是透过帝国理念来看拜占庭的主要问题之一。因为帝国理念在学术中并不仅仅是将拜占庭人抽象的皇权观整理成一套学说；它还被提出作为对政权为何根本会被服从的一种解释。毕竟，任何一套对某一群体的意识形态所作的论述，如果还要全面说明这个群体的政治存在论，都必须能够解释他们的政治行为。否则它就是空中楼阁（而我认为拜占庭宫廷事实上正在建造的恰恰就是这种东西）。
en: In short, if we want to understand why we think what we do about the Byzantine emperor, we need to first understand the political issues that scholars were grappling with in the 1930s and how Byzantium was caught up in them. The 1930s was not a decade like any other when it came to thinking about absolute power, to put it mildly. However, I am not going to carry out such an analysis. My focus here will be on Byzantium. I will be offering an alternative way to understand the “imperial idea” which will expose what the pioneers of the field chose to valorize and what to omit, and what they thought “counted” as political ideology. Scholars in the 1930s were drawn to theocratic ideas, for example, but did not know how to contextualize them. They also did not believe that the actual behavior and decisions of anyone outside the court were relevant. That is one of the main problems of viewing Byzantium through the imperial idea. For the imperial idea is not meant in scholarship to be merely a codification of what the Byzantines thought about the emperor in the abstract; it is offered also as an explanation of why the regime was obeyed at all. Any account of an ideology that is also a comprehensive account of a people’s political ontology must, after all, be able to explain their political behavior. Otherwise it is a castle in the sky (which is what I think the Byzantine court was in fact constructing).

zh: 因此拜占庭学术是分裂的。一方面，它的政治意识形态概念无可救药地是神学性的。另一方面，对皇帝实际赖以治理的那些制度的研究，在取径上是务实的，并不依赖帝国理念来解释多少东西。这些研究谈到帝国理念，是按惯例加上一点背景，但他们对政治事实的分析却基于常识的（且世俗的）权力观念。这些研究很好，却要么根本不对拜占庭政治作理论化，要么不用拜占庭自身的概念来理论化，其原因不难看出：帝国理念的意识形态运作于上帝与皇帝之间的神学空间，而制度则运作于皇帝与其臣民之间的历史空间。人们可以这样来弥合鸿沟：主张皇帝的正当性源于他与上帝的关系，而拜占庭人接受这一点，因而同意制度的运作。换言之，鸿沟是通过
与
这两个概念来闭合的：“皇帝是上帝在世间的代表，人民仅凭这一点就应当服从。”
en: Byzantine scholarship is therefore bifurcated. On the one hand, its concept of political ideology is irredeemably theological. On the other hand, studies of the institutions through which the emperor actually governed are pragmatic in their approach and do not rely on the imperial idea to explain much. They invoke it to give flavor to the context, for it is

but their analyses of political fact are based on common-sense (and secular) notions of power. These studies are good but do not theorize Byzantine politics either at all or in terms of Byzantine concepts, and it is easy to see why: the ideology of the imperial idea operates in a theological space between God and the emperor, whereas the institutions operated in a historical space between the emperor and his subjects. One can bridge the gap by arguing that the emperor derived his legitimacy from his relationship with God and that the Byzantines accepted this and so consented to the operation of the institutions. In other words, the gap is closed through the concepts of
and
“the emperor is God’s representative on earth and obedience is expected from the people for that reason alone.”

zh: 但这一理论通不过最基本的事实检验：拜占庭人，包括精英与君士坦丁堡人民，似乎对于反叛、废黜乃至杀死他们那位神授的统治者几乎毫无顾忌；他们经常这样做。此外，我们无法直接知道他们相信什么，而如果有人质疑他们是否真的“相信”帝国理念——无论那究竟意味着什么——也不清楚能提供什么证据来挽救这一理论。于是意识形态解释不了拜占庭历史，而我们对那段历史的书写又理论不足。帝国理念很齐整，却存在于一个自足的气泡里；与此同时，我们的历史学家在处理权力与争夺的事实时，只能听凭任何在他们直觉上“说得通”的东西摆布。
en: But this theory fails the most basic test of verification: the Byzantines, including both elites and the people of Constantinople, seem to have had little compunction about rebelling against, deposing, and even killing their divinely appointed ruler; they did so regularly. Moreover, we do not have access to their beliefs, and if one were to question whether they did “believe” in the imperial idea—whatever exactly that may have meant—it is not clear what evidence can be provided to salvage the theory. So the ideology does not explain Byzantine history, while our writing of that history is undertheorized. The imperial idea is tidy, but exists in a self-contained bubble; meanwhile, our historians are at the mercy of whatever “makes sense” to them intuitively in dealing with the facts of power and contestation.

zh: 问题在于“信念”这个概念。究竟有没有人真的“相信”帝国理念，那又意味着什么？鉴于我们对拜占庭历史的了解，信奉它似乎不曾让人承担多大的义务。在光谱的一端，我们或许可以提出：它不过是宫廷里几句轻飘飘的说辞，没有人真把它当回事。但这同样解释不了它的无处不在，以及它被看待时的那份庄重。我毫不怀疑，在某个层面上，大多数拜占庭人确实接受帝国理念。问题在于辨认出那个层面。我们或许一开始就不该设想一条单一的信念光谱，一端代表真诚而全心全意的确信，另一端代表“纯粹修辞”或犬儒。我也不会建议把共和国的意识形态放在前者一端、把帝国理念放在后者一端。更可能的是，拜占庭人的思维
沿着若干并不总是相交的轴线运作，因而他们能够维持相互冲突的思维模态，每一种在不同语境中运作，即便它们在理论上彼此对立。我认为这对人类普遍而言是真的，并且与神经科学和进化心理学的发现一致。
en: At issue is the concept of “belief.” Did anyone actually “believe” the imperial idea, and what does that mean? Given what we know of Byzantine history, it cannot have entailed much of a commitment on anyone’s part. At one end of the spectrum, we might propose that it was an airy bit of court rhetoric that no one really took seriously. But this too does not explain its ubiquity and the solemnity with which it was regarded. I have no doubt that, on some level, most Byzantines did accept the imperial idea. The problem is in identifying that level. We should probably not be thinking of a single spectrum of belief in the first place, with one end representing sincere and wholehearted conviction and the other “mere rhetoric” or cynicism. Nor will I be suggesting that we place the ideology of the republic at the former end and the imperial idea at the latter. It seems more likely that the Byzantines’ thinking operated

along different axes that did not always intersect, and so they were able to maintain conflicting modalities of thought, each operating in different contexts even when they were theoretically opposed. I think this is true of human beings generally and consistent with findings in neuroscience and evolutionary psychology.

zh: 例如，想想当时还是候选人的乔治·W. 布什（George W. Bush）在2000年的声明：“我相信上帝想让我当总统，但如果那没有发生，也没关系。”在同一口气里，他既阐明了一套神选理论，
表明了对一种民主程序的承诺——那种程序显然能够推翻神的意志。

布什和大多数人一样，并不怎么关心确保自己的信念前后一致；他的话只是为了让兼具两种身份的听众都能接受：既是福音派信徒、又是选民。他当然“相信”上帝，大概也相信自己注定赢得总统之位，但他的大多数支持者若真到了关头，绝不会接受这样一种想法：这些信念应当压倒既定的选举总统的政治程序（事实上，布什还在那次选举中输掉了普选票）。共和国或民主制中的政治人物，当他们援引上帝来为其具体政策辩护时会招致反对（如布莱尔与伊拉克战争）。但当他们以含糊而抽象的方式呼求上帝时，却会被正面看待。
en: Consider, for example, the statement of then-candidate George W. Bush (in 2000): “I believe that God wants me to become President, but if that doesn’t happen, it’s OK.” In one and the same breath he managed to articulate a theory of divine election
a commitment to a democratic process able, apparently, to overrule the divine will.

Bush was no more interested than most people in ensuring that his beliefs were consistent; he was only saying what made sense to the double-aspected profile of his audience: evangelicals who were also voters. Certainly he “believed” in God, and probably also believed that he was destined to win the presidency, but most of his supporters would have balked at the idea that those beliefs, if it came down to it, should override the established political process for electing a president (and in fact he did lose the election). Politicians in republics or democracies arouse opposition when they invoke God to justify their specific policies (as with Blair and the Iraq War). But they are perceived positively when they call on God in vague and abstract terms.

zh: 在拜占庭——它同样是一个共和国——情形也差不多。“上帝话语”只能在一定程度上、在特定语境中被用作政治论据。现代学术充斥着关于拜占庭人政治神学的绝对化、总体化、不加反思的断言，仿佛它编码了形而上真理，而事实上，和所有历史产物一样，它所表达的立场高度依赖具体处境，应当在它实际发挥作用的那些场合来理解。当它渗出那些语境、进入由另一套规则支配的语境时——比方说，当皇帝把帝国理念带到它本不该运作的地方时——那种脱节便痛苦地显而易见。当伊萨克二世·安格洛斯（Isaakios II Angelos）因搬走教堂珍宝而受责备时，他不耐烦地说，凡事对皇帝都是允许的，因为在逻辑上没有什么能把他们与上帝区分开来。
这是把帝国理念推到了它的断裂点。科尼亚特斯（Choniates）嘲笑他，竟以为上帝会担保并背书他的野心。
同样，普塞洛斯（Psellos）也嘲笑罗曼努斯三世（Romanos III），竟相信既然上帝把皇位给了他，就会在他种种军事与王朝的事业中支持他。普塞洛斯还试图让君士坦丁九世（Konstantinos IX）明白事理，后者断定自己既受上帝保护就不需要卫士（他后来为此遭遇不止一次刺杀企图）。
史家笔下的这些皇帝都沉溺于妄想，但人们也可以说，他们不过是把帝国理念推到了它的逻辑结论，也就是推到了真正“相信”的地步。
en: It was not much different in Byzantium, also a republic. “God-talk” could be used as a political argument only up to a point, and within specific contexts. Modern scholarship is full of absolute, totalizing, and un-reflexive claims about the Byzantines’ political theology, as if it encoded metaphysical truths, when in fact, like all historical artifacts, it was a highly contingent stance that should be bracketed as operating in specific contexts. When it seeped out of them and into contexts governed by a different set of rules, say, when emperors carried the imperial idea into places where it was not supposed to operate, the disjunction was painfully evident. When Isaakios II Angelos was reproached for removing church treasures, he grew impatient and said that all things are permitted to emperors because there was nothing that could logically distinguish them from God.
This was taking the imperial idea to its breaking point. Choniates mocked him for thinking that God would guarantee and underwrite his ambitions.

So too Psellos mocked Romanos III for believing that, since God had given him the throne, he would support him in his various endeavors, military and dynastic. Psellos also tried to talk sense into Konstantinos IX, who concluded that, as he was protected by God, he did not need guards (this led to attempts on his life).
These emperors are presented as delusional, but one could also say that they were merely taking the imperial idea to its logical conclusion, that is, to the point of real “belief.”

zh: 如果上帝不能被用来支持具体政策，那他还有什么用？有趣的是，在表达帝国理念的文本中，上帝明确想要的一件事，就是皇帝勤勉努力以造福其臣民，也就是共和国的核心原则之一。
那么在这个层面上，帝国理念不过是共和义务的一种神学表达。但上帝作为回报给了什么？这就更难衡量了。
en: What good was God if he could not be used to support specific policies? Interestingly, the one thing that God definitely wanted, in texts that express the imperial idea, was that the emperor work hard to benefit his subjects, that is, one of the core principles of the republic.
On this level, then, the imperial idea was but a theological expression of republican obligations. But what did God give in return? This is more difficult to measure.

zh: 一位历史学家最近声称，“既然皇帝的权力被认为来自上帝，那么任何人反对当朝的正当皇帝都是不敬神的。”

这是从他所讨论的文本——帝国颂辞——中作出的一个逻辑推论。但如果他接受那个结论，他就也必须接受逻辑上随之而来的东西，即帝国常常满是不敬神的人，甚至是民众中的大多数。可他不会愿意这么说。为什么不愿意？按照帝国理念的逻辑，叛乱者难道不是被界定为不敬神的吗？然而这里还有一个额外的文本外事实在起作用，即皇帝的统治是否正当，取决于共和国想要什么，而在实践中并不取决于上帝说了什么（我们不可忘记，上帝是一个神学实体，而非历史实体）。总是有人在怀疑皇帝。我们
共和国来解释人们在做什么，因为“帝国理念”解释不了。那么神授之权又当如何？它究竟有什么历史效力？
en: One historian has recently claimed that “since the emperor’s power was thought to come from God, it was impious for anyone to oppose the legitimate emperor of the day.”

This is a logical inference from the texts he is discussing, imperial panegyrics. But if he accepts that conclusion, he must also accept what logically follows, namely, that the empire was often full of impious people, even the majority of the populace. But he would be unwilling to say that. Why not? Were rebels not defined as impious through the logic of the imperial idea? There is, however, an additional extratextual fact in play here, namely, that being “the legitimate emperor” was a function of what the republic wanted and not, in practice, of what God said (who, we must not forget, was a theological, not a historical entity). There was always someone doubting the emperor. We
the republic in order to explain what people were doing, because the “imperial idea” does not. But what then of divine right? What historical valence does it actually have?

zh: 从宏观上看，这种文化并未表现出对神授之权的多少信念。这一点一直为人所知，虽未被解释。同一位学者既可以说“一个人”，即优西比乌，“为帝国其余存续时期的拜占庭政治思想设定了模式”，又可以说“就拜占庭政治生活中被认为没有发言权的大多数人所扮演的角色而言，理论与实践大相径庭。”
那么我们必须由此得出结论：所谓拜占庭政治思想与政治实践几乎无关，这对一个领域来说是一种奇怪的状态。而且，尽管人们轻易地承认现实不同于优西比乌的理论，却除了“个人的野心”之外没有给出任何替代理论来解释那个现实，
仿佛那是某种不在特定文化约束内运作的永恒范畴。如我上文所说，我们尚未用拜占庭自己的概念对这一现实作出理论说明。于是，虽然不难看出“理论有效地掩盖了真实事态”、皇帝事实上是脆弱的，

但我们难道不因此就必须超越修辞、试图揭示支配“真实事态”的实际动力学吗？诉诸“谋杀与阴谋”恰恰暴露了缺失的东西。这类向现实的让步在学术中无处不在。但如果我们的理论无法用拜占庭人可能理解的措辞来解释现实，那它还有什么用？我们需要一个不同的模型，这正是我在拜占庭共和国理论中所提出的。那一理论把拜占庭人作为历史行动者的行为，解释得比大多数学者在导言中公式化地诵念、随后又在分析中弃之不顾而转向“谋杀与阴谋”的那些宗教观念更好。
en: Seen macroscopically, the culture does not evince much belief in divine right. This has always been known, if not explained. The same scholar can say that “one man,” that is, Eusebios, had “set the pattern of Byzantine political thought for the rest of the empire’s existence,” and also that “theory and practice were widely at odds when it came to the role of the voiceless majority in Byzantine political life.”

We must conclude from this, then, that what is called Byzantine political thought had little to do with political practice, which is a peculiar state for a field to be in. And while it is readily conceded that reality was different from Eusebian theory, no alternative theory is given to explain that reality other than “the ambition of individuals,”

as if that were some timeless category that did not operate within specific cultural constraints. As I said above, we have left the reality untheorized in terms of distinctively Byzantine concepts. So, while it is easy to see that “the theory effectively masked the real state of affairs” and that emperors were in fact vulnerable,

are we not then required to go beyond the rhetoric and try to uncover the actual dynamics that governed “the real state of affairs”? Appeals to “murder and intrigue” reveal precisely what is missing. Such concessions to reality are pervasive in the scholarship. But if our theory fails to explain reality in terms that the Byzantines might understand, what good is it? We need a different model, which is what I have proposed in the theory of the Byzantine republic. That theory explains the Byzantines’ actions as historical agents better than the religious ideas that most scholars formulaically recite in their introductions and then discard in their analyses in favor of “murder and intrigue.”

zh: 帝国理念永远解释不了权力的运作，因为它始终是一种事后的神学解释：它跟随历史，而不创造历史。

历史由共和国创造，然后由神学来解释。如果一位皇帝在皇位上稳固，也就是说如果他得民心，那么仅凭这一事实，他也可以被说成是受上帝眷顾的。如果他的地位岌岌可危，那反过来必定意味着上帝正在收回他的眷顾。但最初是什么使皇帝的地位岌岌可危？通常那意味着他不得臣民之心。共和国正在把事情掌握到自己手中，而它无论选谁做继任者——如果真到了那一步——随后都会被视为上帝的宠儿。一位处境危殆的皇帝若援引帝国理念、指望它在如此情形下为他赢得任何支持，那就是傻瓜。在这个意义上，推动事态发展的首先是共和国的政治动向，因为危机时刻，神学并不能左右历史的实际运转。它不过是事后解释共和国所做之事的一种方式；因此它是一种修辞的上层建筑。
此外，正如我们将看到的，拜占庭人并不愿把这两种思考政治领域的方式联系起来，让二者在辩证关系中彼此阐发。它们倾向于保持分离、不可通约，各居其自身的文学与社会生态位。
en: The imperial idea can never explain the workings of power because it was always an ex post facto theological interpretation: it followed history and did not create it.

History was created by the republic and then interpreted by theology. If an emperor was secure on the throne, that is, if he was popular, then by that very fact he could also be said to be favored by God. If his position was precarious, that must conversely have meant that God was retracting his favor. But what made the emperor’s position precarious in the first place? Usually that meant that he was unpopular with his subjects. The republic was taking matters into its own hands, and whoever it chose as a successor, if indeed it came to that, would then be seen as God’s favorite. An imperiled emperor would be a fool to cite the imperial idea and expect it to earn him any support under such circumstances. In this sense, the dynamics of the republic claimed causal primacy, for the theology was in times of crisis disconnected from the gears of history. It was just a way of interpreting after the fact what the republic had done; thus, it was a rhetorical superstructure.

As we will see, moreover, the Byzantines were reluctant to bring these two ways of thinking about the political sphere into conjunction and dialectical exchange. They tended to remain separate and incommensurate, in their own literary and social niches.

zh: 普罗科匹乌斯（Prokopios）在其献给查士丁尼的颂辞《建筑志》（
）中声称，尼卡暴动中的叛乱者起来反对的不仅是皇帝，也是上帝，因为他们烧毁了圣索菲亚大教堂。
当然，他们自己不会这么看：在他们心里，他们是在起来反对一个可恨的僭主，并行使他们宣布拥立新皇帝的权利。
他们高呼。
问题在于他们失败了，于是被打上不敬神叛乱者的烙印。反过来，当1042年民众起来反对米海尔五世（Michael V）时，他们成功了，于是我们的史料急忙在他们的行动背后辨认出神的作为，尽管他们在骚乱中劫掠了修道院。
en: In his panegyric for Justinian, the
Prokopios claimed that the rebels in the Nika riots had risen up against not just the emperor but also against God, for they burned down the church of Hagia Sophia.
Of course, that is not how they would have seen it: in their minds, they were rising up against a hated tyrant and exercising their right to proclaim a new emperor.
they chanted.

The problem is that they lost, and so were branded as unholy rebels. Conversely, when the populace rose up in 1042 against Michael V, they won, and so our sources were quick to discern divine agency behind their actions, even though they looted monasteries during the commotion.

zh: 然而这仍给我们留下一个问题：要解释帝国理念在拜占庭的无处不在与受欢迎，即便就解释推动历史事实的实际动力学而言它意义甚微。是时候把这个阿基米德点相对化，并表明它能撬动的拜占庭世界远比传统所设想的要少。
en: That still leaves us, however, with the problem of explaining the ubiquity and popularity of the imperial idea in Byzantium, even if it meant little in terms of explaining the actual dynamics that propelled the facts of history. It is time to relativize the Archimedean point and show that it can leverage much less of the Byzantine world than has been traditionally assumed.

zh: 帝国理念的兴起与功能
en: The Rise and Function of the Imperial Idea

zh: 那么，为什么皇帝们——不仅他们，还有整个共和国——接受帝国理念作为权力行使的一种理想？完整的答案很可能是多重的，我们应当从许多角度来看这个问题。例如，由于皇帝对生活的方方面面拥有权威、是一切争端的最终仲裁者，他们很快就在基督教共同体的治理中扮演重要角色，甚至在君士坦丁之前就是如此。从四世纪起，他们开始规制教会行政、财政与法律的某些方面，涉及主教的任命、教会大公会议的召集以及教规的实施。异教皇帝曾以祭司身份行事，而他们基督教的继承者需要相当的权威来治理一个迅速成为全球性的基督教共同体。这带来了某些理论问题，归在“皇帝教权主义（Caesaropapism）”的名下：基督教皇帝所需的某种宗教权威并不亚于异教皇帝。我们不应把这看作基督教化的一个结果，而应从皇帝治理其臣民宗教生活所需的权威来看。卡梅伦（Cameron）已经证明，至少直到阿纳斯塔修斯（Anastasios），皇帝们仍保有
（大祭司）的头衔，而且“正是以这一身份他们就教会事务立法。”
由于皇帝并不担任大祭司之职，却又必须高于最高层级的主教，帝国理念便对他们基督教共同体中的至高地位提供了一种含糊得恰到好处的肯定。它把皇帝凸显出来，把他抬高到其帝国如今包含的众多教会主教之上。
en: So why did the emperors, and not only they but the entire republic, accept the imperial idea as an ideal for the exercise of power? The full answer is likely to be manifold, and we should look at the question from many angles. For example, as emperors held authority over all aspects of life and were the ultimate arbiters of all disputes, they quickly came to play an important role in the governance of the Christian community, even before Constantine. Starting in the fourth century, they would regulate aspects of ecclesiastical administration, finance, and law in the appointment of bishops, the convening of Church Councils, and the implementation of the canons. The pagan emperors had functioned in a sacerdotal capacity and their Christian heirs needed comparable authority to govern what was quickly becoming a global Christian community. This posed certain theoretical problems that go under the name of “Caesaropapism”: Christian emperors required some kind of religious authority no less than pagan ones. We should not see this as a function of Christianization but in terms of the authority needed by emperors to govern their subjects’ religious lives. Cameron has demonstrated that emperors down to at least Anastasios retained the title of
and “it was in this capacity that they legislated about church affairs.”

As emperors did not hold pontifical office, but at the same time had to be superior to the highest level of bishop, the imperial idea offered a nicely vague affirmation of their supreme standing in the Christian community. It set the emperor off and elevated him above the many other pontiffs his empire now contained.

zh: 对帝国理念的另一种解释——本节将更详细地展开——是：它试图支撑一个脆弱的君主制，后者在拜占庭政治那场永久革命中随时可能被推翻。
正是政体的共和基础所造成的不稳定，促使宫廷为自己发明出一条正当性的理论原则，它超出共和国各构成部分所能触及的范围，恰恰因为它处于历史之外。按照这一论证，宫廷是在试图改善一种极为危殆的处境，因为如我们所见，臣民一方始终愿意质疑当朝皇帝的正当性。我们可以把这称为“以咄咄逼人的自我主张来掩盖深深的不安全感。”
换言之，把帝国理念看作一条自立而至高的正当性原则的那种通行观点恰恰错了；它其实是对一种远为强大的意识形态力量的防御性回应，而那力量经常
塑造历史。
en: Another explanation for the imperial idea that will be developed at greater length in this section is that it attempted to shore up a fragile monarchy that was liable to be toppled at any point in the permanent revolution that was Byzantine politics.

It was precisely the instability created by the republican foundations of the regime that led the court to invent for itself a theoretical principle of legitimacy that lay beyond the reach of the constituent parts of the republic, precisely because it lay outside of history. According to this argument, the court was trying to ameliorate a desperate and precarious situation, for as we have seen, there was a constant willingness on the part of subjects to question the legitimacy of the current emperor. We might call this “aggressive self-assertion as a cover for deep insecurities.”

In other words, the conventional view of the imperial idea as a self-standing and supreme principle of legitimacy is exactly wrong; it was instead a defensive response to a far more powerful ideological force, a force that regularly
shape history.

zh: 我在此赶紧抢先排除一个可能的误解：拜占庭并非在共和力量与神权力量之间被撕裂，更不是在派系或政党之间。如我们所见，
与
双方都接受政体的共和框架，而我们将看到，

都有兴趣在修辞—宗教层面上维持帝国理念。换一种说法：皇帝们是共和主义者，而人民是基督教君主制的信徒。而且没有人有兴趣去暴露帝国政权的系统性弱点。人民也想要一位强大的皇帝，只要他合他们的心意。“服从皇帝——直到你决定推翻他！”无论对统治者还是臣民都不可能成为一条权力教义。这两种力量——共和的与神权的，一个是意识形态的、另一个是修辞的——之所以和平共存，是因为它们在相当不同的层面上运作、履行互补类型的工作：神权说辞为共和政治所造成的现实处境提供了缓冲。要看清这一点，我们需要考察帝国理念在晚期古代的起源，以便解释它的功能，从而限制它的运作范围与存在论范围。它从来不是罗马政体赖以自治的一种“意识形态”（如第1章所定义）。它是一种修辞性的损害控制模式，兴起于三世纪，此后被保留下来，部分原因在于拜占庭政治本质上始终有爆发革命的可能，尤其是当皇帝们定居君士坦丁堡、它变得更具共和性之后。为了解释帝国理念作为对日益加剧的不稳定之反应而起源，本节将首先聚焦三、四世纪的材料，那时神权与共和之间那种独特的拜占庭平衡被锻造出来。
en: I hasten here to head off a potential misunderstanding: Byzantium was not torn between republican and theocratic forces, far less factions or parties. As we saw,
the court
the populace accepted the republican framework of the polity, and we will see that

had an interest in maintaining the imperial idea on the rhetorical-religious level. To put it differently, the emperors were republicans and the people were believers in Christian monarchy. And no one had an interest in exposing the systemic weakness of the imperial regime. The people too wanted a strong emperor, so long as he was to their liking. “Obey the emperor—until you decide to overthrow him!” could not be a doctrine of power for either rulers or subjects. The reason why these two forces—republican and theocratic, the one ideological and the other rhetorical—peacefully coexisted is because they operated on quite different levels to perform complementary types of work: the one rhetorically ameliorated the reality created by the other. To see this we need to survey the origin of the imperial idea in late antiquity in order to explain its function and thereby restrict its operational and ontological scope. It was never an “ideology” (as defined in Chapter 1) by which the Roman polity ever governed itself. It was a mode of rhetorical damage control that emerged during the third century and was retained thereafter in part because Byzantine politics was essentially a state of perpetual potential revolution, especially when it became more republican after the emperors settled in Constantinople. In order to explain the origin of the imperial idea as a reaction to increasing instability, this section will focus initially on material from the third and fourth centuries, when the distinctively Byzantine balance between theocratic and republican was forged.

zh: 从 J. R. 菲尔斯（J. R. Fears）对古代神选观念的综述中浮现出一个引人注目的印象：它通常被援引来支撑一种有被视作不正当之风险的权威，例如在内战或统治的剧烈更迭之后。
随着奥古斯都身后的人们渐渐忘却此前的暴力，“对超自然正当化的需求减少了”。

但在灾难性的三世纪发生了一次重大转变，那时帝国秩序经历了一场持续的正当性危机。从三世纪初到四世纪末，皇帝大多随军队在外征战，不与元老院和罗马人民保持常规接触，这破坏了正常的正当化过程。诚然，在罗马传统中军队可以充当共和国的代表机构、从而使一次即位正当化，但三世纪有太多军队同时在这样做。在这个意义上，直到皇帝们重新定居新罗马、并逐渐让整个共和国重新参与确认皇权正当性。我们考察的491年阿纳斯塔修斯获选一事，已体现了这一变化，共和国才恢复稳定。然而在此期间，皇帝们已发展出种种神选观念。此前那不过是诸策略中的一种，而且或许只运用于文学文本而非官方宣告。
许多历史学家已出色地勾勒出三世纪晚期发展的进程。“随着帝国的危机在三世纪中叶加深，皇帝们更充分地诉诸修辞，变成不可征服的将军，其战争行动彰显了一位独一至大之神的支持与意志。”

在其他修辞策略失败之后，这一点加剧了，并自奥勒良（Aurelian，270–275年在位）起大力推行。许多学者已表明神选如何从异教版本变异为基督教版本，从奥勒良与“不可征服的太阳”（Sol Invictus）的关联，到戴克里先与马克西米安（Maximian）同其守护神朱庇特、赫拉克勒斯的个人认同，再到马克森提乌斯（Maxentius）与马尔斯的关联，最终轮到君士坦丁——他在转向基督教上帝（无论他认为那是谁）之前，曾尝试阿波罗与“不可征服的太阳”。
雷·范·达姆（Ray Van Dam）对君士坦丁的宗教转变提出了一种挑战旧说的解释：不是对基督教的发现与接受，而是一系列持续的战略举措，旨在先把他自己、继而把他正在兴起的王朝，与其政治对手——四帝共治及其继承者——那种特定的神学自我呈现区别开来。
en: A striking impression that emerges from J. R. Fears’s survey of the idea of divine election in antiquity is that it was usually invoked to bolster an authority that was at risk of being perceived as illegitimate, for example, after a civil war or a dramatic change of rule.
“The need for supernatural legitimation grew less” as the violence was forgotten after Augustus.

But a significant shift occurred in the disastrous third century, when the imperial order experienced a sustained crisis of legitimacy. From the beginning of the third century to the end of the fourth, the emperors were mostly with the armies in the field and not in regular contact with the senate and the people of Rome, and this destabilized the normal processes of legitimation. To be sure, in Roman tradition the armies could act as representative bodies of the republic and thereby legitimate an accession, but too many armies were doing this simultaneously during the third century. In this sense, stability was not restored to the republic until the emperors settled back down in New Rome and gradually drew the entire republic back into the process of legitimation (by 491, as we saw in the election of Anastasios). In the meantime, however, emperors had developed various notions of divine election. Previously that had been one strategy among others and perhaps deployed only in literary texts rather than official proclamations.

Many historians have ably charted the course of the late third-century developments. “As the empire’s crisis deepened in the middle years of the third century, emperors resorted more fully to rhetoric, becoming unconquerable generals whose actions in war demonstrated the support and manifested the will of a single greatest god.”

This intensified after other rhetorical strategies had failed and began in force with Aurelian (270–275). Many scholars have shown how divine election mutated from pagan to Christian versions, passing from Aurelian’s association with Sol Invictus to the personal identification of Diocletian and Maximian with their patron deities, Jupiter and Hercules, then to Maxentius’s association with Mars, and finally to Constantine, who experimented with Apollo and Sol Invictus before turning to the Christian God (whoever he thought that was).

Ray Van Dam has provocatively reinterpreted Constantine’s religious shifts not as a discovery and acceptance of Christianity but as ongoing strategic moves designed to set off first himself and then his emerging dynasty from the specific theological self-presentation of his political rivals, the Tetrarchy and its heirs.

zh: 某些结论浮现出来，而它们在对帝国理念去语境化的诵念中并不明显。第一，帝国理念起源于一场系统性的正当性危机，那场危机由军事失败与不稳定、以及皇帝们离开罗马这两方面因素共同造成。在罗马，元老院与人民能够赋予他们正当性，也就是“任何统治者必须满足、才能让臣民感到自己正被恰当权威治理的那些条件。”
据此，“神选是一种危机的意识形态。”

但作为一种修辞策略，即便在皇帝们回到首都（新罗马）之后它仍被保留，并在那里与共和意识形态的模式与秩序融合。因此，帝国理念在危机中的起源支持了这样一个论点：即便在拜占庭时代，它的功能也是缓解君主制固有的不稳定。神权观念由那些需要把自己置于军队一时兴之所不能及之处的皇帝们所首创。当一些士兵试图发动革命时，奥勒良告诉他们，若以为皇帝的命运掌握在他们手中，那就是自欺；因为神已把紫袍给了他（他用右手举起它），并已指定了他统治的时候。
此外，帝国理念并非独特的基督教之物。我们在优西比乌那里发现的，不过是一个异教与基督教皇帝已试验数十年的观念的一种可能变体。

就它们在政治领域中的功能而言，并无本质区别。对优西比乌的固着、以及把他抬高为某种拜占庭奠基者，掩盖了其中基本观念的非原创性，并强化了历史学家喜欢在罗马与神权拜占庭之间设定的那种人为分野。事实上，“帝国理念”是由奥勒良、戴克里先、君士坦丁这样自觉的罗马爱国者锻造出来的。它是一种罗马式的危机回应，只是在君士坦丁治下才获得了一副基督教面孔。在更晚近的时代，历史学家不太相信那次过渡中有什么根本性的东西改变了：“基督教只是略微改变了皇帝神圣性质的来源。”
en: Certain conclusions emerge that are not apparent in decontextualized recitations of the imperial idea. First, the imperial idea originated as a response to a systemic crisis in legitimacy that was caused by a combination of military defeat and instability and the departure of the emperors from Rome. At Rome the senate and people could endow them with legitimacy, that is, “the conditions any ruler must satisfy in order for subjects to feel they are being governed by proper authority.”
Accordingly, “divine election was an ideology of crisis.”

But as a rhetorical strategy it was retained even after the emperors returned to the capital (New Rome), where it fused with the modes and orders of republican ideology. Therefore, the imperial idea’s origin in crisis supports the case that even in Byzantine times it functioned to ameliorate the monarchy’s systemic instability. The theocratic idea was pioneered by emperors who needed to place themselves beyond the reach of the armies’ whim. When some soldiers attempted a revolution, Aurelian told them that they were deluding themselves if they thought that the fate of emperors was in their hands; for God had given him the purple (he held it up in his right hand) and had appointed the time for him to reign.

Moreover, the imperial idea was not distinctively Christian. What we find in Eusebios is only one possible variation of a notion with which pagan and Christian emperors had been experimenting for decades.

There was no essential difference when it came to their function in the political sphere. The fixation on Eusebios and his elevation as some kind of Founder of Byzantium has obscured the unoriginality of the basic ideas involved and has reinforced the artificial divide that historians like to postulate between Rome and theocratic Byzantium. In fact, the “imperial idea” was fashioned by self-conscious Roman patriots such as Aurelian, Diocletian, and Constantine. It was a Roman response to crisis that only acquired a Christian face under Constantine. In more recent times, historians are less likely to believe that something fundamental changed in the transition: “Christianity only slightly altered the source of the emperor’s sacred quality.”

zh: 毕竟，君士坦丁擅长“把罗马与基督教的线索交织在一起”，使每一者都显得像是另一者。
en: Constantine, after all, was adept at “intertwining Roman and Christian threads,” making each appear as the other.

zh: 我们需要停止依赖1933年对优西比乌的那些解释，更不该让它们成为现代解读拜占庭政治领域的核心。一旦某些观念在一个领域里根深蒂固，就很难看清它们基于什么，而晚近研究已挑战了优西比乌作为“君士坦丁的神学理发师”的形象。
例如，A. 约翰逊（A. Johnson）论证说，优西比乌并不认同罗马帝国秩序，也不在他的历史观中给它一个特殊位置。那套让历史学家如此全神贯注的“政治神学”，在他早期著作中并不存在，而是晚期为解释一位基督教君主可能是什么而作的尝试。
优西比乌其实是逐步发展出他的帝国神学的：起初他也把君士坦丁的崛起归于军队，继而归于军队与上帝，最后才只归于上帝，而这一转变部分是他试图粉饰那场军事政变的丑陋现实的结果。

那么从一开始，优西比乌式的理念就只是应对罗马帝国政治现实的另一种方式，而那些现实并非由理念本身预先决定。更令人不安的是雷·范·达姆发出的有力警告：不要把优西比乌的政治神学读作规范性的；他关于君士坦丁的著作是他试图支撑其从属论（不符合尼西亚信经）神学的一种方式。这牵涉到模糊耶稣与君士坦丁作为上帝在世间的行动者之间的区别。如果说“君士坦丁挪用耶稣的生平来服务于他的政治目标，那么优西比乌则挪用君士坦丁的生平来服务于他的神学目标。”
仔细阅读其著作的拜占庭人会质疑它们的正统性，而且事实上优西比乌那些论君士坦丁的著作在拜占庭似乎并不受欢迎，拜占庭对它们持怀疑态度。
总而言之，有许多理由停止把优西比乌当作拜占庭思想的开国元勋来对待。
en: We need to stop relying on interpretations of Eusebios from 1933, far less make them central to modern readings of the Byzantine political sphere. Once certain ideas become ingrained in a field it is difficult to see what they are based on, and recent studies have challenged the image of Eusebios as “Constantine’s theological hairdresser.”

For example, A. Johnson has argued that Eusebios did not identify with the Roman imperial order or give it a special place in his view of history. The “political theology” that has so preoccupied historians is not found in his early works and was a late attempt to explain what a Christian monarch could be.

Eusebios in fact developed his imperial theology gradually: at first he too had attributed Constantine’s rise to the army, then to the army and God, then finally to just God, and in part this shift was a result of his attempt to ameliorate the ugly reality of what was in fact a military coup.

Right from the start, then, the Eusebian idea was only another way of coping with the realities of Roman imperial politics, realities that were not predetermined by the idea itself. More troubling is the powerful warning issued by Ray Van Dam against reading Eusebios’s political theology as normative: his writings about Constantine were a way by which he tried to prop up his subordinationist (non-Nicaean) theology. This entailed blurring distinctions between Jesus and Constantine as agents of God on earth. Whereas “Constantine appropriated Jesus’ life to serve his political goals, Eusebios appropriated Constantine’s life to serve his theological objectives.”

Byzantines who read his works closely would have questioned their orthodoxy, and in fact it does seem that Eusebios’s Constantinian writings were not popular in Byzantium, which was skeptical of them.
All told, there are many reasons to stop treating Eusebios as the Founding Father of Byzantine thought.

zh: 三世纪的军人皇帝发展出神选观念，部分是为了把皇帝职位与那种由哗变军队进行选举的混乱绝缘开来。在实践中，军队那时在大多数权力过渡中扮演主要角色，除非某位皇帝已设法把自己的意志强加于他们、并操纵继承。为此创造出最稳定框架的那些皇帝，也正是赋予自己种种形式神圣权威的那些人，即戴克里先与君士坦丁，尽管如今已无法查明这些“神权”观念通过什么机制、在多大程度上影响了军队的决定。我们不知道罗马军队如何作决定。很可能他们只被成功所打动，而神权—帝国理念是皇帝们保留并投射一种成功光环的方式。这样一来，皇权的正当性便同时得到了两套解释。一方面，按照共和国的规范，皇帝通过军队（武装的罗马人民）的欢呼获得正当性；另一方面，按照悬浮于这些交易之上的修辞，他们又不知怎么地由某位神任命来统治。有趣的是，没有人试图在理论上协调这两种立场。它们在各自的领域里都“管用”，而这显然就够了。
en: The military emperors of the third century developed the notion of divine election partly to insulate the imperial office from the chaos that was election by mutinous armies. In practice, the armies were then playing the major role in most transitions, unless an emperor had managed to impose his will on them and steer the succession. The emperors who created the most stable frameworks for this were also those who invested themselves with various forms of divine authority, that is, Diocletian and Constantine, though it is impossible to ascertain now by what mechanisms and to what degree these “theocratic” ideas influenced the armies’ decisions. We do not know how Roman armies made decisions. It is likely that they were impressed only by success, and the theocratic-imperial idea was a way for the emperors to retain and project an aura of success. This led to an overdetermination of imperial legitimacy. On the one hand, according to the norms of the republic, emperors derived legitimacy through acclamation by the army (the Roman people at arms), while, on the other hand, according to the rhetoric that hovered over these transactions, they were also somehow appointed to rule by some deity. It is interesting that no one sought to reconcile these two positions theoretically. They both “worked” in their respective spheres, and apparently that was sufficient.

zh: 即便在皇帝们定居新罗马、并由民众（或由军队与民众，或由共和国的代表）任命之后，神权观念与共和观念仍继续在平行轨道上运作。如上文所论，拜占庭中期的君主制比晚期古代的军人皇帝更具共和性。但没有出现一个统一的理论模型来协调皇权这两种不可通约的来源。例如，人们本可以主张上帝的意志显现在人民的选择之中（
，人民之声即上帝之声），但拜占庭人并未发展出一套理论来说明这如何运作、或上帝为何通过这样的工具来运作。没有一种历史神学，也没有一个《旧约》模型能帮助把两者关联起来。
我们的史料至多把两个选项混在一起，却不告诉我们它们如何相关。阿纳斯塔修斯在即位时感谢共和国的众多构成要素把他抬上皇位，然后加了一个关于“神圣三位一体之善意”的独立属格从句。
查士丁一世（Justin I）在即位时声称自己“凭全能上帝的裁断与你们一致的表决”获得了君主之位。
查士丁尼在其法律中既声称罗马
由上帝托付给他，
声称皇权源于
六世纪匿名的《论政治科学》（
）说皇权“由上帝给予、由公民提供”，尽管在别处它只提公民或只提上帝。
最后再举一个拜占庭中期的例子：尼基弗鲁斯三世·博塔内亚特斯（Nikephoros III Botaneiates）责备叛乱者布里恩尼奥斯（Bryennios）藐视那使他博塔内亚特斯成为皇帝的上帝恩典，继而暗示布里恩尼奥斯本应从这样一个事实中领会上帝的意志：当他的军队逼近城墙时，君士坦丁堡人民拒绝了他。
这种结合太含糊：我们无从得知一个权威来源如何通过另一个运作（无论朝哪个方向）。要是不听民众怎么说，人又怎能知道上帝是否改变了意志？那是否意味着人民在其政治选择上基本不会犯错？那是否意味着上帝通过那些违背对他所发誓言的叛乱来运作——也就是说，只要叛乱者成功？“没有文本就神意显现自身或被传达的过程给出明确细节，”
而我们能明白为什么，鉴于这样一个文本为了弥合这两种不可通约的思维模式所必须克服的挑战。
en: The theocratic and the republican ideas continued to operate on parallel tracks even after the emperors settled down in New Rome and were appointed by the populace (or by the army and the populace, or the representatives of the republic). As argued above, the monarchy was more republican in the middle Byzantine period than the military emperors had been in late antiquity. But no unified theoretical model emerged to reconcile the two incommensurate sources of imperial authority. One might have argued, for instance, that the will of God was manifested in the people’s choice

but the Byzantines did not develop a theory as to how this worked, or why God was working through such instruments. There was no theology of history and no Old Testament model that might help correlate the two.

At most our sources lump the two options together, without telling us how they were related. At his accession, Anastasios thanked the many constituent elements of the republic for elevating him to the throne and then added a genitive absolute clause on the “good will of the Holy Trinity.”
At his accession, Justin I claimed to have received the monarchy “by the judgment of almighty God and your universal vote.”
In his laws, Justinian claimed both that the Roman
had been entrusted to him by God
that imperial authority stemmed from the
The sixth-century anonymous
says that imperial authority “is given by God and offered by the citizens,” though elsewhere it mentions only the citizens or only God.

To close with a random example from the middle period, Nikephoros III Botaneiates reproached the rebel Bryennios for flouting the grace of God that had made him, Botaneiates, emperor and then implies that Bryennios should have learned the will of God from the fact that the people of Constantinople rejected him when his armies approached the walls.

The conjunction is too vague: we do not learn how one source of authority operated through the other (in whichever direction). How would one know whether the will of God had changed independently of what the people were saying? Did it mean that the people were basically infallible in their political choices? Did it mean that God worked through rebellions in which oaths to him were broken—so long, that is, as the rebel was successful? “No text gives explicit details concerning the process by which the divine will manifested itself or was communicated,”
and we can see why, given the challenges that such a text would have overcome in order to bridge these two incommensurate modes of thought.

zh: 这是一个真正的问题。拜占庭人对上帝思考良多，并已发展出一套相当繁复的关于其本性及其在历史中作用的理论。然而他们从未解释为什么他会选择以这样一种方式来任命他在世间的副手。可以说，任何构建一个神权—帝国政权的人，都不会选择把一切都建立在平民主义—共和原则的运作之上。很清楚，我们在此面对的是一个政治领域，其根本的、先在的意识形态框架是共和的，其上叠加了一套神权修辞。前者关乎塑造所有相关行动者行为的那些前提（他们对权力在统治者与被统治者之间如何运作的直觉理解），后者关乎他们喜欢如何想象其政治秩序在尘埃落定后的最佳状态。帝国理念绝没有以任何方式挑战或质疑人民以欢呼拥立皇帝、又以呼声否定他的举动：恰恰相反，它赋予他们的行动以神圣的有效性。
（人民）也希望自己的选择被说成得到上帝的认可，也就是说，只要神意是事后运作的。
en: This is a real problem. The Byzantines thought a lot about God and had developed a fairly elaborate theory about his nature and role in history. Yet they never explained why he would choose to have his deputy on earth appointed in such a way. Arguably no one constructing a theocratic-imperial regime would choose to premise everything on the operation of populist-republican principles. It is clear that we are dealing here with a political sphere whose fundamental and preexisting ideological framework was republican, onto which had been superimposed a theocratic rhetoric. The first had to do with the premises that shaped the behavior of all the agents involved (their intuitive understanding of how power worked between rulers and ruled), the second with how they liked to imagine their political order in its optimum state once the dust had settled. It is not as though the imperial idea in any way challenged or questioned what the people had done in their acclamations and deacclamations: to the contrary, it gave their actions divine validity. The
too wanted its choices to be cast as divinely approved, so long, that is, as the divine will operated in retrospect.

zh: 一些学者已认识到拜占庭帝国传统中这种正当性的“双轨”，
但它的存在使解释这种文化的尝试变得棘手。一些学者先解释皇帝如何由人类的“选举人”产生，然后又单独讨论帝国理念，却不表明两者如何相关。
这会产生奇怪的效果。想想艾卡特琳·赫里斯托菲洛普卢（Aikaterine Christophilopoulou）的著作。在她那部关于皇帝选举与任命的权威综述中，她几乎忘了帝国理念，只是把它作为事后补充加上，尽管称它为“一个本质要素”。但如果它是这样一个本质要素，为什么在她对制度与事件的长篇分析中它却不占一席之地？即便她确实提到它，她也基本上把它当作面向公众的一套说辞。
另一方面，在一部关于拜占庭国家的通论性著作中，她提供了一种自上而下的取径，用惯常的神权观念来界定皇帝的位置。
因为她不提
，并从绝对皇权这个阿基米德点出发，她就能把皇帝必须为其臣民利益而统治这一观念，当作对他权力的一种
，而不是当作权力的定义与目的本身。这是一个常见的错误，由帝国理念把皇帝置于与共和国其余部分相隔的那种虚幻孤立所产生。
en: Some scholars have recognized this “dual track” of legitimacy in the Byzantine imperial tradition,

but its existence has made attempts to explain the culture problematic. Some scholars first explain how the emperors were created by human “electors” and then separately discuss the imperial idea, without showing how the two were related.

This can have peculiar effects. Consider the work of Aikaterine Christophilopoulou. In her magisterial survey of the election and appointment of the emperors, she almost forgets the imperial idea, adding it as an afterthought albeit calling it “an essential element.” But if it was such an essential element, why does it not feature in her long analysis of the institutions and events? Even when she does mention it, she treats it basically as mere public relations.
On the other hand, in a general book on the Byzantine state, she offers a top-down approach that defines the imperial position in terms of the usual theocratic notions.
Because she does not mention the
and begins from the Archimedean point of absolute imperial power, she can take the idea that the emperor had to rule on behalf of his subjects as a
on his power rather than as its very definition and purpose. This is a common mistake produced by the illusory isolation in which the imperial idea places the emperor from the rest of the republic.

zh: 另一些学者似乎想发明他们自己的“大统一理论”，例如诉诸西方那个套语
（人民之声即上帝之声）。但这并不出现在拜占庭史料中，
而且这种取径的问题还要更深。创造弥合共和国与上帝的理论，模糊了这样一个事实：它们运作于不同的历史、修辞、乃至认知层面；它们不应被相互转换与同质化。然而，几乎没有历史学家甚至做到那一步，因为大多数人略去或没有意识到共和维度，或者认为它在晚期古代已太过微弱、在拜占庭更是如此。萨宾·麦科马克（Sabine MacCormack）在《晚期古代的艺术与仪式》（

children: Art and Ceremony in Late Antiquity

zh: ）中极为出色地再现了帝国仪式所传达的理想，但也犯了这个错误。她把文本中的神学说辞当成所研究的人群深层的意识形态（这一举动得益于当时晚期古代研究中正在发生的“宗教转向”）。因此，尽管她的文本常常暗指共和国的意识形态，她却几乎只聚焦宗教维度。她甚至把人民的作用贬为一种“准虚构”
（仿佛帝国理念不是一种
虚构），并延续了把拜占庭看得比晚期古代帝国更神权的错误（于是她惊讶于“皇帝由人民选举这一要素从未被丢弃”）。
但有时她确实把帝国理念看作一种改善罗马帝国运作方式所造成紧张的办法。例如，她提出帝国理念使各种掌权者得以在一次有争议的选举之后投射出一种共识。
这是一个很好的建议。帝国理念是一个修辞空间，所有相关各方都能在其中不失面子地表明他们愿意支持政权——直到他们选择不支持。再一次，共和国产生结果，然后帝国理念试图控制损害、掩盖紧张，并为已发生之事摆出最好看的面孔。
en: Other scholars seem to want to invent their own “grand unified theories,” for example, by having recourse to the western trope
But this does not appear in Byzantine sources,

and the problem with this approach is deeper still. Creating theories that bridge the republic and God blurs the fact that they operated on different historical, rhetorical, and indeed cognitive levels; they should not be interconverted and homogenized. However, few historians even do that because most omit or are not aware of the republican dimension, or think that it was too attenuated in late antiquity and even more so in Byzantium. This is true of Sabine MacCormack’s otherwise brilliant evocation of the rhetorical ideals associated with imperial ceremonies, in

children: Art and Ceremony in Late Antiquity.

en: She accepts the theological rhetoric of the texts as the deep-seated ideology of her subjects (a move facilitated by the “religious turn” taking place at that time in the study of late antiquity). Therefore, while her texts often allude to the ideology of the republic, she focuses almost exclusively on the religious dimension. She even dismisses the role of the people as a “quasi-fiction”
(as if the imperial idea were not a

fiction) and perpetuates the mistake of seeing Byzantium as more theocratic than the empire of late antiquity (so she is surprised that “the element of the emperor’s election by the people was never dropped”).

But sometimes she does see the imperial idea as a way to ameliorate the tensions caused by the ways in which the Roman empire operated. For example, she suggests that the imperial idea enabled the various holders of power to project a consensus after a contentious election.

This is a good suggestion. The imperial idea was a rhetorical space in which all relevant parties could, without loss of face, signal their willingness to support the regime—until they chose not to. Again, the republic produced the results and the imperial idea then tried to contain the damage, hide tensions, and put the best face on what had happened.

zh: 某些申言帝国理念的文本如此具有防御性，以致我们可以把那句格言用到它们身上：“凡未被官方否认之事，切勿相信。”例如，一位颂辞作者声称，“
人们偶然的同意，也不是某种出乎意料的声望爆发，使你成为皇帝。”
另一位声称，“
以为士兵是这样一个重大任命的主人；毋宁说，选举自上而下。”
“是上帝把这个地位给你，
“皇帝
从人那里、或通过人接受他的冠冕，而是从上帝那里。”
一位皇帝亲自作出这些否认，强调使他成为皇帝的
众人的手、或武器、或演说，而是主的右手。
那么这够得上一个修辞
（套语）。它以它自己的方式，旨在弥合皇帝们在不同语境中所享有的共和与神权两种权力主张之间的理论鸿沟。若要用这些说辞理解历史，就必须认识到它们揭示了对两者关系的一种深深焦虑：神权那一者始终有被共和那一者削弱的危险，在实践中与理论上皆然（故有不断的否认）。这些否认试图反驳的，恰恰是人人心里认为已经发生的事。当 G. W. 布什声色俱厉地宣称伊拉克战争“
白打”时，他的声明事实上揭示精英与广大民众中很大一部分人恰恰已经认为这场战争是白打了。“对任何权威的肯定，越是在该权威受到严重质疑时，越趋于变得尖厉。”
颂辞演说，若在其直接历史语境中研究，往往可被看作短期的危机管理。有时它们未能凝聚支持。
en: Some of the texts asserting the imperial idea are so defensive that we can apply to them the adage “Never believe anything until it is officially denied.” For example, one panegyrist claimed, “
random agreement of men, nor some unexpected burst of popularity, made you emperor.”
“Do
think that the soldiers were the masters of such a momentous appointment; rather, the election comes down from above,” claimed another.
“God is giving you this rank,
“The emperor does
receive his crown from men, or through men, but from God.”
One emperor made these denials himself, stressing that it was
the hands of the many, or weapons, or speeches that had made him emperor, but the Lord’s right hand.
This, then, qualifies as a rhetorical

In its own way, it aimed to bridge the theoretical gap between the republican and the theocratic claims to power that emperors enjoyed, albeit in different contexts. If we want to convert these statements into history, we have to realize that they are revealing a deep anxiety about the relationship between the two: the theocratic was always in danger of being undermined by the republican, in practice as well as in theory (hence the constant denials). The latter were trying to counter precisely what everyone was thinking had happened. When G. W. Bush stridently proclaimed that the Iraq war had “

been in vain,” his statement in fact reveals that large parts of the elite and the population at large had come to believe exactly that. “The affirmation of any authority tends to become shriller the more seriously that authority is contested.”
Panegyrical orations, studied within their immediate historical context, can often be seen as short-term crisis-management. Sometimes they failed to rally support.

zh: 让我们退后一步，把我们的结论放进视野。拜占庭是一个共和的、而非“宪制的”君主制。虽然没有人民得以行使权力的常规法律机制，却也没有任何正式协议能在皇帝激怒人民或共和国其他要素、后者诉诸法外措施时保护皇帝免受罢黜等处置。革命是共和国针对个别皇帝行动的永久却非常规机制。拜占庭的政治在君主制的“常态”与共和革命之间摆动，而在每一种状态中，所有人都把眼睛盯着另一种。对叛乱最好的防护是声望。
en: Let us step back and put our conclusions into perspective. Byzantium was a republican and not a “constitutional” monarchy. While there were no regular legal mechanisms by which the people could exercise power, there were also no formal agreements that could shield an emperor from the anger of the people or other elements of the republic when they had recourse to extralegal measures. Revolution was the permanent but irregular mechanism by which the republic acted against individual emperors. Politics in Byzantium oscillated between monarchical “normalcy” and republican revolution, and in each state everyone had their eyes fixed on the other. The best protection against rebellion was popularity.

zh: 王朝原则永远无法永久扎根，因为人民随时可以再行主张共和原则，改变王朝继承。正如塔西佗（Tacitus）那句名言所宣告的，

奥古斯都之后不久秘密就泄露了：皇帝可以在任何地方被造就，而最终他们也可以凭一时兴之所至被废掉。正是在这些情形下，三世纪末四世纪初的皇帝们制定出关于其帝国地位的神学观念，其功能是使皇位摆脱极不稳固的处境，使皇帝们能够有权威地治理。帝国理念当然不担保保护，但它可能提高了那些考虑叛乱者的门槛。然而很难衡量它成功的程度：我们对臣民为何在那些时候反叛皇帝知之甚少；而他们为何在没有反叛时没有反叛，则根本无从知道。所以我们无法衡量帝国理念在稳定这一制度方面相对于其他变量的有效性（例如，戴克里先与君士坦丁也保护帝国抵御外敌，并且总体上是受欢迎的皇帝）。
en: The dynastic principle could never take permanent hold because it could always be undone by a reassertion of the republican option. As Tacitus famously declared,

the secret was out soon after Augustus that emperors could be made anywhere, and eventually that they could be undone on a whim. It was in these circumstances that emperors at the end of the third and the beginning of the fourth century formulated theological notions of their imperial status whose function was to elevate the institution out of the radical insecurity in which it was mired and enable the emperors to govern with authority. The imperial idea did not guarantee protection, of course, but it may have raised the bar for those considering rebellion. It is hard, however, to measure the degree of its success: we know little about why subjects rebelled against emperors when they did; it is impossible to know why they did not when they did not. So we cannot measure the effectiveness of the imperial idea at stabilizing the institution compared to other variables (for example, Diocletian and Constantine also protected the empire against foreign enemies and were generally popular emperors).

zh: 罗马传统只授权为共和国利益而使用权力。但从帝国之初，皇权就是非常规而难以界定的。最终，一旦秘密泄露，它也变得危殆，而“公开把行政首脑说成跑腿小厮是不明智的，因为伤害行政首脑的自尊会减损他的用处。”
这正是帝国危机中发生的事，那时皇帝们被抬上来以满足某支外省军队的一时兴致，然后又同样迅速地被废掉。这就是奥勒良和戴克里先正是在这种局势中成长起来的。但所有罗马人都想要一个有用、稳定而强大的行政首脑，尽管他们也主张在权力过渡中有发言权。帝国理念及其相关的仪式装置，是一种尝试的组成部分，旨在把皇帝重新塑造成一种更稳定、更崇高、甚至神圣的权力的执行者：“仪式给委婉化赋予一种貌似可信的气派。”
尽管如此，帝国理念从未取代拜占庭罗马政治的共和基础，也没有任何证据表明它本应如此。
en: The Roman tradition authorized the use of power solely in the interests of the republic. But from the start of the empire, imperial power was irregular and hard to define. Eventually it also became precarious, once the secret was out, and it is “unwise to speak openly of the executive as an errand boy, for to hurt the executive’s pride would diminish his utility.”

This is what happened in the crisis of empire, when emperors were elevated to satisfy the whims of some provincial army, and then just as quickly deposed. This was the context in which both Aurelian and Diocletian matured. But all Romans wanted a useful, stable, and powerful executive, though they also claimed the right to have a say in the transition of power. The imperial idea and its associated ceremonial apparatus were parts of an attempt to recast the emperor as the executive of a more stable, exalted, and indeed divine power: “ceremonial gives euphemization an air of plausibility.”
Still, the imperial idea never displaced the republican foundations of Roman politics in Byzantium, nor is there any evidence that it was supposed to do so.

zh: 大多数拜占庭人持有两套信念，尽管在不同语境中。他们相信皇帝由上帝任命来统治，
相信他们自己有权废黜他
算不敬神。效忠誓言神圣不可侵犯，
在皇帝是“僭主”也就是不得民心时被置之不顾。他们相信皇帝凭神恩统治，
相信他由人民任命：尽管他们无法解释神恩为何竟会选择以那种方式运作，他们却希望自己的选择被铸为上帝的选择。拜占庭人由衷地为自己的君主感到宗教上的自豪，积极参与颂扬他们，
随时准备相信他们最坏的一面，在街头辱骂他们、暴动、煽动叛乱。那么他们至少有两种“信念”模态，而这两者似乎并不彼此沟通。和所有人一样，拜占庭人能够在不同语境中转而采用另一套行为准则和“信念”，取决于一整套复杂的社会规范、情境约束与心理需求，其中很少是我们能重新捕捉的。
en: Most Byzantines held both sets of beliefs, albeit in different contexts. They believed that the emperor was appointed to rule by God
that they themselves had the right to depose him
impiety. Oaths of loyalty were sacrosanct
were ignored when the emperor was a “tyrant,” that is, unpopular. They believed that the emperor ruled by divine grace

that he was appointed by the people: even though they had no way to explain why divine grace would ever choose to operate in that way, they wanted their choice to be cast as the choice of God. The Byzantines were religiously proud of their monarchs, taking an active part in their exaltation,

were ready to believe the worst about them, reviling them in the streets, rioting, and fomenting rebellions. They had, then, at least two modes of “belief,” which seem not to have been in communication with each other. Like all people, the Byzantines could switch between codes and “beliefs” in different contexts, depending on a complex array of social norms, situational constraints, and psychological needs, few of which we can recapture.

zh: 在心理学与认知科学中，人们理解到人类能够同时相信相互矛盾的东西，每一种都在一个于心理或社会上有利的语境中变得活跃，而不觉得有必要把它们拿来比较、为其不一致而困惑。这不是某种失调，而是对大多数人（与文化）在大多数时候倾向于如何运作的一种描述。例如，帝国理念似乎在拜占庭人把自己与外国人相比时、或他们对政权感到信心时被打开，也就是当正当性已由共和国各要素创造出来时。当他们想评价他、考虑自己的选项时——同样是作为共和国成员——它就被关掉。它的目的是促成某些关系，并为它们提供一个宫廷与人民都觉得有利的模板——在某些情形下。当情形改变、人民按另一套假设行动时，他们未必也觉得有必要把它们表述出来。这部分就是为什么我们有一个被过度理论化的理想和一个理论不足的现实。
en: In psychology and cognitive science it is understood that human beings can simultaneously believe contradictory things, each one becoming operative in a context in which it is psychologically or socially advantageous, without feeling the need to compare them and be puzzled about their inconsistency. This is not some kind of disorder but a description of how most people (and cultures) tend to operate most of the time. The imperial idea, for example, seems to have been switched on when the Byzantines compared themselves to foreigners or when they felt confidence in the regime, that is, when legitimacy had been created by the elements of the republic. It was switched off when they wanted to evaluate him and consider their options, again as members of the republic. Its purpose was to facilitate certain relationships and provide a template for them that the court and the people found advantageous—under certain circumstances. When circumstances changed and the people acted on a different set of assumptions, it is not necessary that they also felt the need to articulate them. That is in part why we have an overtheorized ideal and an undertheorized reality.

zh: 牧首佛提乌（Photios，九世纪）为我们提供了这种情境逻辑的许多例子，它们提示我们应当转向一种模块化、情境化的模型来思考拜占庭政治中的世俗与宗教。例如，佛提乌在蛮族某次进攻期间想凝聚他的信众时，把蛮族呈现为野蛮的异教徒；而当他想因信众不够虔诚而羞辱他们时，又把他们呈现为值得效仿的虔诚高贵的异教徒。
不同语境与不同修辞目标引出了相互矛盾的立场。那么，在一篇以书信形式写成的短论中，佛提乌提出了一个关于国家起源的彻底
论证，它在若干实质方面偏离了颂辞文本所表达的帝国理念——后者把罗马人的帝国看作一件用于人类救赎的神圣工具。佛提乌在此直率地声明，
en: The patriarch Photios (ninth century) provides us with many examples of this situational logic, which suggest that we should turn to a modular and situational model for thinking about the secular and the religious in Byzantine politics. For example, Photios presented barbarians as savage heathens when he wanted to rally his flock during one of their attacks, but as pious noble pagans worthy of emulation when he wanted to shame his flock for not being religious enough.
Different contexts and different rhetorical goals elicited contradictory positions. Well, in a short treatise cast in the form of a letter, Photios presented a radically

argument for the origin of states that deviated in substantial ways from the imperial idea expressed in panegyrical texts, which viewed the empire of the Romans as a divine instrument for the salvation of mankind. Here Photios states bluntly that:

zh: 我们的救主、我们的上帝无意建立政治政权或其任何秩序。因为他知道，他清楚地知道，人类能够凭自己的经验建立这些制度，日常所遇的实际需要自然会教会他们如何去做，而前人的错误将防止后代犯同样的错误……救主的意图只关乎灵魂的救赎。
en: our Savior and God had no intention to establish political regimes or any of their orders. For he knew, he knew well, that human beings would be able to provide these things for themselves from their own experience, that necessity would easily furnish them with instruction on a daily basis, and that the errors of those who came before would prevent future generations from making the same mistakes... The Savior’s intention was only a concern for the salvation of souls.

zh: 这是怎么回事？是什么促使这位拜占庭牧首否定基督教对于罗马帝国的奠基作用，把帝国视为人类从试错中逐渐改进的成果？对罗马帝国的基督教解释在此被表明只在修辞与仪式语境那有限的空间里繁荣。在那个气泡之外，存在相互竞争的主张与解释。这正是佛提乌发现自己所处的困境：他被人要求反驳皇帝尤利安（Julian）的论证，其中之一是基督教对政治理论或国家的建立毫无贡献，包括罗马国家——尤利安坚持说，它是由异教徒建立的。
这就是为什么佛提乌退回到“灵魂的救赎”，并把国家的建立归于纯粹人类那种自行摸索。当他补充说耶稣也没有为军事战术、市场监察官与法官立下规定时，他转向了讥讽。
他像伊索的狐狸一样，嘲弄并贬低他得不到的东西。在别的情形下，他能够对帝国政权的方方面面投射一种彻底神学的解释。然而我们在此看到，只要修辞语境需要，一种关于国家起源的世俗观点对他而言也并非不可及。这里是另一个例子：在1080年代，“一些拜占庭人提出上帝只关心人的灵魂，而他们的政治事务是运气之事。”
他们的思维模式是情境性的，这应当告诫我们不要把帝国理念当作任何人关于帝国政治本性的固定信念。可供选择的思维方式有很多。
en: What is going on? What caused this Byzantine patriarch to renounce the Christian claim to the Roman empire and cast it as the work of men improving through trial and error? The Christian interpretation of the Roman empire is here shown to have flourished only in the limited space of rhetorical and ceremonial contexts. Outside of that bubble there were competing claims and interpretations. This is exactly the predicament Photios found himself in: he had been asked to refute the arguments of the emperor Julian, among which was that Christianity had contributed nothing to political theory or the foundation of states, including the Roman one, which, Julian insisted, had been founded by pagans.

That is why Photios falls back on “the salvation of souls” and attributes the foundation of states to the uninspired fumbling of mere human beings. He turns to sarcasm when he adds that Jesus also did not lay down prescriptions for military tactics, market inspectors, and judges.

He mocks and trivializes what he cannot have, like Aesop’s fox. In other circumstances, he could project a thoroughly theological interpretation of every aspect of the imperial regime. We see here, however, that a secular view of the origin of states was also not beyond him, so long as it was required by the rhetorical context. Here is another example: in the 1080s, “some Byzantines were suggesting that God was only interested in men’s souls, and that their political affairs were a matter of fortune.”

Their modes of thinking were situational, and this should caution us against treating the imperial idea as anyone’s settled belief on the nature of imperial politics. There were many ways of thinking available.

zh: 世俗共和国
en: The Secular Republic

zh: 拜占庭艺术史家的材料大多属宗教性质，他们近年来却更愿意质疑那种铁板一块的虔诚文化形象。安东尼·卡特勒（Anthony Cutler）指出，“只在一个神话般的拜占庭——它总被设想为普遍而坚定不移地虔诚——里，圣经戏仿的概念才是不可想象的。”
在《别样的圣像》（
）中，亨利与尤妮斯·马圭尔（Henry and Eunice Maguire）窥视“拜占庭人为自己如此成功地创造的那副金色庄严外表的背后，以揭示另一个世界。拜占庭的这个另一个世界以新奇与矛盾为乐，颂扬鲜血与暴力，以着迷的目光看待裸体与不受拘束的身体动作。”
艾丽西亚·沃克（Alicia Walker）观察到，她的领域常常强调拜占庭艺术中的基督教因素，却忽略外来因素，而她假定存在“一个老练而知情的受众，他们会思考得超出官方意象那套视觉陈词滥调、及其关于通过神圣认可确保的不变普世统治的信息。”
en: Byzantine art historians, whose material is mostly of a religious nature, have been more willing in recent years to question the image of a monolithically pious culture. Anthony Cutler has noted that “only in a mythical Byzantium, always supposed to be universally and unwaveringly devout, is the notion of a biblical parody inconceivable.”
In

Henry and Eunice Maguire peer “behind the façade of golden solemnity that the Byzantines so successfully created for themselves, to reveal another world. This other world of Byzantium delighted in novelty and contradiction, glorified blood and violence, looked with fascination on nudity and on abandoned movement.”

Alicia Walker observes that her field has often played up the Christian elements in Byzantine art and missed the exotic ones, and she postulates the existence of “a sophisticated and informed audience, who would have thought beyond the visual platitudes of official imagery and its message of unchanging universal dominion secured through divine endorsement.”

zh: 相比之下，拜占庭的社会、政治与思想史家却不愿假定受众能够看穿那些陈词滥调，尽管这类学者能接触到一大批并不由宗教关切主导的史料。一个例外是汉斯-格奥尔格·贝克（Hans-Georg Beck），他写了一部关于拜占庭情欲的书，论证教父们关于这个题目可能说过的任何话，对于理解这种文化如何运作大都无关紧要。

如我们所见，贝克也开创了看待拜占庭政治的“罗马”方式。奇怪的是，他开辟的两条路径都没有被进一步探索。为什么我们没有其他关于拜占庭性观念与性行为的书？材料绰绰有余。关于帝国理念，贝克说，很难形成它对人们心灵支配力的印象，因为现代学术对它太过轻信。但可以从材料中看出，拜占庭时代许多宣扬帝国理念的人自己也对它心存怀疑（尤其是当他们后来转向历史学家时，如普塞洛斯与科尼亚特斯）。“人民对这类哲学—神学思辨的关注，远少于今天大多数学者所相信的。”
en: By contrast, Byzantine social, political, and intellectual historians have been reluctant to assume that audiences could have seen past the platitudes, even though such scholars have access to a broad array of sources that are not dominated by religious concerns. An exception was Hans-Georg Beck, who wrote a book on Byzantine eroticism arguing that anything that the Church Fathers might have said about the topic is largely irrelevant for understanding how the culture worked.

As we have seen, Beck also pioneered “Roman” ways of looking at Byzantine politics. It is odd that neither of the avenues he opened up has been explored further. Why do we have no other books on Byzantine sexuality? There is more than enough material. About the imperial idea, Beck said that it is difficult to form an impression of its power over people’s minds because modern scholarship is too trusting of it. But many of its own spokesmen in Byzantium can be shown to have been skeptical of it (especially when they later turned historian, such as Psellos and Choniates). “The people paid far less attention to such philosophical-theological speculations than most scholars believe today.”

zh: 总体上有很多材料可以说明拜占庭的世俗思维方式，但学术在我们与它之间竖起了壁垒。让我们回到保罗·亚历山大1962年那篇论拜占庭人眼中“帝国之力”（Strength of Empire）的经典文章，一部被频繁引用、仍在重印的著作。这篇文章包含许多错得惊人的陈述，其中有些之所以出错，是因为亚历山大愿意从有限证据中得出一般性的否定结论。
沿着这条思路他还提出了一个已被证明有影响力的论点：“拜占庭人把他们帝国与都城的伟大归于他们的超自然保卫者，因此几乎没有动力去发展一种对其伟大的历史分析、或一种关于其政治发展的世俗理论。”
我们不应试图通过在某种特殊意义上理解“分析”与“理论”来挽救这一断言。亚历山大当时所说、以及他随后被认为所说的，无非是拜占庭人没有能力、或没有兴趣以世俗方式思考。这一理论在此后数十年间不断回响。引几位领头历史学家的话：“在他们公共与私人存在的方方面面，拜占庭人所做之事都用神意来解释，并诉诸上帝的意志与设计来正当化。”
另一位学者援引关于非洲的人类学研究，把拜占庭人归类为“不分享西方因果概念”的人，他们虽然可能能够理性思考，却更愿意把事件归于恶魔或上帝。
还能引更多。
这些观念然后被非专家接手、重新铸成如下样子：“拜占庭人以一种在基督教世界历史上几乎无与伦比的强度过着他们的精神生活。”
en: There is plenty of material generally to illustrate secular ways of thinking in Byzantium, but scholarship has erected barriers between us and it. Let us go back to Paul Alexander’s classic article from 1962 on the “Strength of Empire” as seen by the Byzantines, a work that is cited often and still reprinted. This article contains many spectacularly wrong statements, which in some cases go wrong because Alexander was willing to draw general negative conclusions from limited evidence.

Along these lines he also produced a thesis that has proven influential: “The Byzantines attributed the greatness of their empire and capital to their supernatural defenders and therefore had little incentive to develop either a historical analysis of their greatness or a secular theory of their political development.”

We should not try to save this claim by taking “analysis” and “theory” in a special sense. What Alexander was saying, and what he was subsequently taken to have been saying, was no less than that the Byzantines were incapable or uninterested in thinking in secular terms. This theory has echoed through the decades since. To quote some passages from the leading historians: “In every aspect of their public and private existence, what the Byzantines did was explained in terms of divine providence and justified by recourse to God’s will and design.”

Another scholar invokes anthropological studies of Africa to classify the Byzantines as people “who do not share western concepts of causation” and who, while possibly able to think rationally, preferred to attribute events to demons or to God.
More can be cited.
These notions are then picked up by nonexperts and recast as follows: “The Byzantines lived their spiritual life with an intensity hardly matched in the history of Christendom.”

zh: 这些陈述在我看来并未公正对待拜占庭社会，更未公正对待它的知识分子——后者正是这里主要针对的对象。听起来仿佛一套陈词滥调在被重复翻炒，却从未充分对照证据检验过。例如，领头的中世纪学家苏珊·雷诺兹（Susan Reynolds）论证说，那种认为中世纪人不可能有无神论的既定观念，并不符合中世纪的心态，却可能算得上一种现代学术的
（心态）。
只看得见一种证据，是一种偏见。拜占庭作家关于他们的国家及其成功的原因有很多话要说。其中有些是宗教的、有些是世俗的，取决于体裁、文本的需要、以及作者那一刻的眼光。我们并不总能解释模态切换，但我们必须承认它们的存在。例如在一处，查士丁尼说“我们
把信任放在武器、士兵、我们的军事将领或我们的才干上，而是把全部希望寄托于至高三位一体的眷顾。”
但在另一处他断然声明“健全的政府依赖两样东西，武器与法律”，而在第三处他从历史角度论证罗马帝国的基础是由法务官的法律与武器奠定的。
我要再次提请读者注意虔敬版本那种防御性修辞：
我们的武器或士兵，这揭示他预期大多数读者恰恰会想到武器与军队。悖论正是由此获得力量，因为查士丁尼的统治比任何其他统治都更由法律与武器所界定。如果他把这套说法贯彻到底、解散军队、只信靠祈祷，他的臣民会以为他疯了。照现状看，它只有修辞价值：我
信靠上帝，信到愿意说出某种我们都知道是疯狂的话（但我会保留我的军队与法律）。
en: These statements do not seem to me to do justice to Byzantine society, and even less to its intellectuals, who are the ones mostly targeted here. It sounds as if a set of clichés is being recycled without ever having been tested fully against the evidence. Susan Reynolds, a leading medievalist, has argued for instance that the established notion that people in the Middle Ages were incapable of atheism is not true of medieval mentalities but may count as a type of modern scholarly

The ability to see only one type of evidence is a prejudice. Byzantine authors had a lot to say about their state and the reasons for its success. Some of it was religious and some of it secular, depending on the genre, the needs of the text, and the author’s outlook at that moment. We cannot always explain modal switches, but we have to recognize their existence. In one passage, for example, Justinian says that “we do
place our trust in weapons, soldiers, our military leaders, or our talents, but rest all our hopes in the providence of the Supreme Trinity.”

But in another place he states categorically that “sound government depends on two things, arms and laws,” while in a third he argues historically that the foundations of the Roman empire were laid by the laws and arms of the praetors.
I would again draw attention to the defensive rhetoric of the pietistic version:

our weapons or soldiers, which reveals that he expected most of his readers to think precisely of weapons and armies. That is how the paradox gains its force, for Justinian’s reign was defined more than any other by laws and arms. If he were to take his claim to its conclusion and disband the armies, trusting in prayer alone, his subjects would think that he had gone mad. As it stands, it has only rhetorical value: I
trust in God, so much so that I am prepared to say something that we all know is insane (but I will keep my armies and laws).

zh: 然而在大多数拜占庭学术中，修辞—宗教模态被视为本质而首要的，并被照字面接受为对整个文化的界定，而世俗模态则被贬到边缘、被归入宗教模态之下、或被斥为不存在。正如哈尔登（Haldon）所论证的，
en: In most Byzantine scholarship, however, rhetorical-religious modalities are regarded as essential and primary and taken at face value as definitive of the culture as a whole, while secular ones are relegated to the margins, subsumed under the religious ones, or labeled nonexistent. As Haldon has argued,

zh: 只有在基督教的语汇之中、并通过它——它描述了东罗马世界的“象征宇宙”——查士丁尼及其同时代人才能理解他们的世界、在其中行动，进而改变这个世界……政治因此总是“宗教的”，而宗教总是“政治的”……以现代术语在“宗教”与“政治”或“世俗”之间强加一种区分，实在太容易了。
en: It was only in and through the vocabulary of Christianity, which described the “symbolic universe” of the East Roman world, that Justinian and his contemporaries were able to apprehend their world and act in and upon it... Politics are thus always “religious,” and religion is always “political”... it is all too easy to impose a division between “religious” and “political” or “secular” in modern terms.

zh: 然而我们的学术有它自己分裂的模态逻辑。当它界定拜占庭思想的
参数时，它紧贴“基督教的语汇”，但当它试图解释政治如何运作时，它又常常暗示拜占庭人是基于世俗假设而行动的。
en: Yet our scholarship has its own bifurcated modal logic. When it is defining the

parameters of Byzantine thought it sticks closely to “the vocabulary of Christianity,” but when it is trying to explain how the politics worked, it often implies that the Byzantines were acting on the basis of secular assumptions.

zh: 例如，哈尔登与布鲁贝克（Brubaker）那部关于圣像破坏时代拜占庭的里程碑式历史，（按通行做法）把皇权界定为一件神学之事，并提出拜占庭人唯一地以宗教方式理解事件。
于是他们对利奥三世（Leon III）崛起的分析令人惊讶：“他之所以得到皇位，可能很大程度上是因为他能够有效地把自己呈现为一位有能力应对阿拉伯威胁的能干将军。”

作者们事先没有给我们任何提示，说存在一个公共舆论的论坛、其中进行着这类“呈现”，也没有任何关于精英或民众会以怎样的政治观念对这些说法作出回应的说明。读者在此不得不想象一整片公共与私人辩论的竞技场，其中宗教与世俗的考量争相吸引注意。我们难道就被指望假定世俗因素反正都在起作用，仅仅因为，说到底，拜占庭人也和我们一样是人？这个领域两头占便宜：它通过把拜占庭人弄得在宗教上与所谓“现代”心态迥异来抬高自己的人类学资历，同时又假定那些心态理所当然地在起作用；无需把它们带进理论。
en: For example, Haldon and Brubaker’s monumental history of Byzantium in the Iconoclast era defines imperial authority (conventionally) as a theological matter and suggests that Byzantines understood events exclusively in religious terms.

Their analysis of the rise of Leon III thus comes as a surprise: “he may have owed his throne largely to the fact that he could present himself effectively as an able general capable of dealing with the Arab threat.”

The authors have given us no prior warning that there was a forum of public opinion in which such “presentations” were made or any sense of the ideological receptivity of the elite or populace to them. The reader here has to imagine a whole arena of public and private debate, of religious and secular considerations jostling for attention. Are we just meant to assume that secular factors were in play anyway because, come on, they were only people after all? The field has it both ways: it plays up its anthropological credentials by making the Byzantines seem religiously alien to allegedly “modern” mentalities, all the while assuming that those mentalities were in play as a matter of course; no need to bring them into the theory.

zh: 历史学家把世俗那一面视为当然，而在其纲领性陈述中突出宗教方面。但这给出了一种文化的偏颇图景，因为帝国理念只有置于一个总体上按世俗因素运作的政治领域之中才说得通——在那个领域里，利奥的军事能力（相对于潜在竞争者的能力）能够显得是使他成为皇帝的一个有力论据，对那些在一个独特的共和政治竞技场内有务实选择要作的“选举人”而言。
en: Historians take the secular side for granted and highlight the religious aspects in their programmatic statements. But this gives a lopsided view of the culture, because the imperial idea only makes sense within the context of an otherwise secular political sphere, a sphere where Leon’s military capabilities (as opposed to those of potential competitors) could seem to be a strong argument for making him emperor to “electors” who had pragmatic choices to make within a distinctively republican political arena.

zh: 没有哪部书比 G. 达格龙（G. Dagron）那部在其他方面才华横溢的《皇帝与祭司》（
）更能体现这些挑战，许多人把它看作关于皇帝地位的定论。这部分是由于英文版那个具有欺骗性的全面而雄心勃勃的副标题（
，《拜占庭的皇帝职位》；原副标题准确得多：

，《拜占庭皇帝教权主义研究》）。达格龙所做的是追溯单一问题的历史，即那种挥之不去的怀疑：皇帝是某种神圣人物。他的阐述极为出色，但必须把它放进视野。几乎没有什么拜占庭人、也许只有寥寥数人，可以被表明关心这个问题，而有许多他想强行纳入这一主题服务的时刻似乎并不属于它（例如，每当一位皇帝表现出谦卑或悔改，他就把这当作皇帝因为自己暗中享有祭司性质的权能，而在教士面前深感不安的标志）。有时达格龙给人的印象是他在触及拜占庭心灵的深层，但另一些时候他承认他处理的只是寥寥几部文本。
这部书因此被关于《旧约》平行与模型的讨论所主导。达格龙对他所略去的东西是坦率的，尽管只是顺带一提：“帝国独立于皇帝们而存在……以罗马那种庞大行政与司法建构的形式，君主支配它、确保它的凝聚，却从未完全与它等同。”
虽然他知道皇帝有一个“庞大的”罗马面向，他却不处理它。他的书对皇帝大多数时间在做什么、或他们如何被臣民评价只字不提。由于这种遮蔽，他得以得出结论：皇帝们若不是人民与上帝之间天意的中介就什么都不是，因此只能就其职位的祭司方面被抵抗；
想必，他们在
是不可触及的。然而事实上，我不知道有
时候一位皇帝因其祭司僭称而处于危险。达格龙回避历史史料，专注于少数
曾以“祭祀之王”（或类似）面目揭示皇帝的仪式。
en: No book exemplifies these challenges better than G. Dagron’s otherwise brilliant
which many regard as the last word on the position of the emperor. In part this is due to the deceptively comprehensive and ambitious subtitle of the English edition (
the original subtitle was much more accurate:

). What Dagron does is trace the history of a single issue, the lingering suspicion that the emperor was some kind of sacral figure. His exposition is superb, but it has to be put in perspective.
