Few Byzantines, perhaps only a handful, can be shown to have been concerned with this issue, and there are many moments that he wants to press into the service of this theme that do not seem to belong (for example, whenever an emperor shows humility or repentance he takes this as a sign of his bad conscience before the clergy over the “secret” of his sacerdotal qualities). Sometimes Dagron gives the impression that he is tapping into deep levels of the Byzantine mind, but at other times he admits that he is dealing with only a handful of texts.

The book is accordingly dominated by a discussion of Old Testament parallels and models. Dagron is candid, albeit in passing, about what he has elided: “the empire existed independently of the emperors... in the Roman form of a vast administrative and juridical construction which the sovereign dominated and whose cohesion he ensured without ever becoming entirely identified with it.”

While he knows that there was a “vast” Roman side to the emperor, he does not deal with it. His book has nothing to say about what emperors did for most of the time or how they were evaluated by their subjects. As a result of this occlusion he can conclude that the emperors, being nothing if they were not the providential mediators between people and God, could be resisted
regarding the sacerdotal aspects of their office;
presumably, they were
beyond reach. In reality, however, I do not know of
time when an emperor was in danger because of his sacerdotal pretensions. Dagron avoids historical sources, concentrating on a few ceremonies that
have revealed the emperor in the guise of a “king of the sacrifices” (or the like).

zh: 于是，虽然我们仍缺乏一部关于拜占庭皇帝职位的研究，那种印象却被强化了：皇帝必须主要作为一个宗教人物、在与教会的关系中来研究。甚至在达格龙的书之前，麦科马克在《晚期古代的艺术与仪式》（

children: Art and Ceremony in Late Antiquity

zh: ）中就引用了皇帝祭司功能的证据，以得出结论：“在早期拜占庭区分世俗与教会领域是误导性的，因为这种区分无法牢固地锚定于证据。”
这取决于“牢固”意味着什么。在此它似乎意味着“在每一个可能的情形中、毫无歧义实例”，那是一个太高的标准。此外，即便表明皇帝既是宗教统治者又是世俗统治者的证据，也未必意味着一般性的区分
被作出；毋宁说，它只意味着在皇帝这个情形中它们
，因为他兼有两种权威。事实上，世俗与教会之间的区分能够相当好地“锚定于证据”。我以举例的方式提供一个场所，其中罗马—政治与基督教—教会被拜占庭人清楚地区分开来，即他们对皇帝的评价。
en: So while we still lack a study of the imperial office in Byzantium, the impression has been reinforced that the emperor must be studied primarily as a religious figure, in relation to the Church. Even before Dagron’s book, in

children: Art and Ceremony in Late Antiquity

en: MacCormack had cited evidence for the emperor’s sacerdotal functions in order to conclude that “it is misleading to distinguish between the secular and the ecclesiastical spheres in early Byzantium, for the distinction cannot be firmly anchored in the evidence.”

This depends on what “firmly” means. In this case it seems to mean “in every possible case with no instance of ambiguity,” which is too high a standard. Besides, even evidence that shows that the emperor was both a religious and a secular ruler does not necessarily mean that general distinctions
made; rather, it means only that in the case of the emperor they

because he combined both types of authority. In fact, the distinction between the secular and the ecclesiastical can be “anchored in the evidence” quite well. I offer by way of illustration a site where Roman-political and Christian-ecclesiastical were clearly distinguished by the Byzantines, namely, in their evaluation of emperors.

zh: 对众多皇帝工作表现的评价区分了世俗与教会领域，尤其是当从作者的立场看两者之间有值得注意的偏差时（他们的判断正确与否无关紧要；第一个尤其异想天开）。君士坦提乌斯二世（Constantius II）是个阿里乌派异端，却对臣民怀有善意、裁判公正、生活节制、任命官职审慎。
尤利安因其背教被许多基督教作家谴责，然而他们承认他作为统治者展现出良好品质，并且“对共和国是必要的”。
阿纳斯塔修斯也擅长“公共事务的管理”（πολιτικὰ πράγματα 的 διοίκησις），但在宗教信仰方面（δόξα εἰς τὸ θεῖον）却不好。
利奥五世（Leon V）“在宗教事务上不敬神”，却是“公共事务的一位非常能干的行政者”、“罗马共和国的一位大功臣”。
狄奥菲洛斯（Theophilos）作为圣像破坏异端与迫害者被谴责，却因其作为统治者的公正及其宏伟建筑而受赞扬。
他死后，其遗孀塞奥多拉（Theodora）试图确保他获得赦免，提醒那些他曾迫害的修士：“你们都知道他是多么公正的一位法官、他把一切治理得多么好（πάντα καλῶς διοικῶν），但他曾持有这种异端信仰，临终前已经弃绝了它。”
（恺撒）巴尔达斯（Bardas）处理国家事务精力充沛，但没有人会说他对教会好。
有趣的是，皇帝图拉真（Trajan）在拜占庭被奉为模范皇帝，后人也没有明确地把他塑造成基督徒。
en: Evaluations of the job performance of numerous emperors distinguished between the secular and the ecclesiastical spheres, especially when there were noteworthy deviations between the two from the author’s standpoint (whether their verdicts were correct or not is beside the point; the first one is especially fantastic). Constantius II was an Arian heretic but was well intentioned toward his subjects, just in his verdicts, restrained in his life style, and careful in making appointments to offices.
Julian was condemned for his apostasy by many Christian writers, yet they conceded that he exhibited good qualities as a ruler and was “necessary to the republic.”
Anastasios was also good at the “management of public affairs” (διοίκησις of the πολιτικὰ πράγματα), but not good when it came to his religious beliefs (δόξα εἰς τὸ θεῖον).
Leon V was “impious in religious matters” but “a very competent administrator of public affairs” and “a great provider to the Roman republic.”
Theophilos was condemned as an iconoclast heretic and persecutor but praised for his justice as a ruler and his magnificent buildings.

After his death, his widow Theodora tried to secure his absolution by reminding the monks whom he had persecuted that “you all know what a just judge he was and how well he governed everything (πάντα καλῶς διοικῶν), but he had this one heresy, which he renounced as he was dying.”
The
Bardas was energetic in handling the affairs of state, but no one would call him good for the Church.
Interestingly, the emperor Trajan was upheld in Byzantium as a model emperor without being overtly Christianized.

zh: 那种认为拜占庭世俗与宗教事务之间

区分的观点，要求拜占庭人分不清宗教事务与非宗教事务，这是不可信的。他们关于什么是、什么不是宗教的看法当然随时间转变，或在任何一个时刻都可能被争论，但今天同样如此。这并不意味着他们在自己生活的语境中总体上分不清。诚然，主张两者之间有一种范畴性的区分、它们被严格而绝对地分开，也同样不可信。没有人主张“分离”，那是一种规范性理想，而非概念区分。没有理由相信普通拜占庭人作不出这样一种区分。它不是某种只有受过教育者才能获得的秘传教义。很可能它是民众持续对每位皇帝评价的基础。在这一点上我们必须重访罗马
，并记住关于它与基督教共同体及教会关系的一些基本事实。
en: The view that there

distinction between secular and religious matters in Byzantium requires that the Byzantines could not tell the difference between religious matters and nonreligious matters, which is implausible. Their view of what was and was not religious certainly shifted over time, or may have been debated at any one time, but the same is true today. It does not mean that they could not tell the difference, by and large, in the context of their own lives. To be sure, it would also be implausible to maintain that there was a categorical distinction between the two, that they were kept strictly and absolutely separate. No one is arguing for “separation,” which is a normative ideal, not a conceptual distinction. There is no reason to believe that average Byzantines could not make such a distinction. It was not some esoteric doctrine available only to those with an education. It is likely that it was basic to the ongoing popular assessment of each emperor. At this point we must revisit the Roman
and remember some basic facts about its relation to the Christian community and the Church.

zh: 罗马政体成为基督教政体，有赖于特定的历史条件，而这也在这两个共同体——罗马的与基督教的——之间造成了一种概念上的不对称：它们至多能重叠，却不同一，因为它们是不同
的共同体，由不同的标准集界定。早期基督教作家，包括优西比乌与诸如纳齐安的格列高利（Gregorios of Nazianzos）这样的教父，曾写到罗马人与基督徒属于不同的
（政体）、拥有不同的法律（人定法与神法）。
“只有从四世纪初起我们才能把基督教描述为罗马宗教。”
但即便那时，过渡也是崎岖的，留下了永久伤疤。戴克里先和其他共治皇帝曾在大迫害中试图使他们的宗教成为全帝国所有罗马人的规范，也就是把它与“做一个罗马人意味着什么”的定义本身挂钩。
他们失败了。伽列里乌斯（Galerius）是第一位使基督教成为罗马人可接受宗教选项的皇帝，而这一结合被君士坦丁进一步推进，可能遵循了他宫廷教师拉克坦提乌斯（Lactantius）的哲学。后者的《神圣原理》（
）是一项调和罗马与基督教
的庞大努力，
一项并不容易、也从未完全成功的努力。我将在另一项研究中论证，在拜占庭基督教与罗马仍是概念上相异的范畴。尽管它们在实践中常常重叠，却有太多反复而永久的提醒它们差异的东西，使拜占庭人永远无法忘记它。任何知道一点历史、或曾去过教堂的人都知道罗马人曾经不是基督徒。而且虽然拜占庭大多数罗马人是基督徒，却并非所有基督徒都是罗马人。
en: The Roman polity was only accidentally Christian, and this too created a conceptual asymmetry between the two communities, Roman and Christian: they could at most overlap but were not identical because they were different

of communities, defined by different sets of criteria. Early Christian writers, including Eusebios and Church Fathers such as Gregorios of Nazianzos, had written about Romans and Christians belonging to different
and having different sets of laws (human and divine).
“It is only from the early fourth century that we can describe Christianity as Roman religion.”

But even then the transition was rough and left permanent scars. Diocletian and the Tetrarchy had tried in the Great Persecution to make their religion normative for all Romans throughout the empire, to link it, that is, to the very definition of what it meant to be a Roman.

They failed. Galerius was the first emperor to make Christianity an acceptable religious option for a Roman, and this union was taken further by Constantine, possibly following the philosophy of his court professor Lactantius. The latter’s
were a massive effort to harmonize the Roman and Christian

an effort that was not easy or ever entirely successful. I will argue in a separate study that Christian and Roman remained conceptually distinct categories in Byzantium. For all that they often overlapped in practice, there were too many recurring and permanent reminders of their difference for the Byzantines ever to forget it. Anyone who knew any history or ever went to church knew that the Romans were once not Christians. And while most Romans in Byzantium were Christians, not all Christians were Romans.

zh: 提到两套法律、两个
，指向今天所称的教会—国家关系问题。这是一个巨大的议题，我不打算在此进入。
我们缺乏一部关于拜占庭这个问题的基础研究，
而且似乎也没有持续的讨论。在这个意义上，达格龙的《皇帝与祭司》通过使问题脱轨而阻塞了此处的进一步讨论：达格龙不去考察制度在实践中如何运作、或关于神圣与世俗界线何在的辩论，反而把这一领域的注意力转向一个冷僻的题目，即皇帝的神圣身份。他的结论本身如此秘传，以致许多学者宁愿干脆回避这个问题，也不愿被缠进它们之中。我知道这一点，因为我就是其中之一。但事实仍然是，我们有如此多的文本声明
是世俗的、
属于教会。我再提几个，以反驳那种“区分无法牢固地锚定于证据”的假定。
en: Mention of the two sets of laws, the two
points to what today is called the problem of Church-State relations. This is a huge issue which I do not intend to enter here.
We lack a basic study of the question for Byzantium,
and there does not appear to be an ongoing discussion either. In this sense, Dagron’s

has blocked further discussion here by derailing the question: rather than examine how institutions functioned in practice, or the debates over where the line lay between sacred and secular, Dagron diverted the field onto the esoteric topic of the emperor’s sacred persona. His conclusions are themselves so esoteric that many scholars would rather just avoid the question than get tangled up in them. I know this because I am among them. But the fact remains that we have so many texts which state that
is secular and
belongs to the Church. I will mention a few more to counter the assumption that “the distinction cannot be firmly anchored in the evidence.”

zh: 这种区分有时被随意地作出，因为它通常被视为当然。它不需要巨大的概念飞跃。随机举几个例子：君士坦丁区分了教会内部的纷争与“外部”世界的纷争。
佛提乌说历史学家塞尔吉乌斯（Sergios）既报道了
的事件、也报道了
（教会）的事件。
作家们也区分不同类型的权威——世俗的与教会的——及其各自的承担者；这是一种基于法律的区分。
神圣法，即教会大公会议的教规，在理论上区别于帝国法，即便皇帝选择批准前者、从而赋予它帝国权威；利奥六世称它们为
（神圣之事）与
（政治之事）。
普塞洛斯经常区分从事公共事务的（πολιτικώτερα）与追求灵修的（πνευματικώτερα）生活方式。
奥赫里德的塞奥菲拉克托斯（Theophylaktos of Ohrid，或其修辞人格）在其《为宦官辩护》（
）中，把古代皇帝那些禁止阉割男子使之成为宦官的法律斥为“世俗的”（κοσμικὴν）、“由此世统治者所启发的”。他们的目标是增加
的人口、拥有更多士兵。相比之下，君士坦丁废除了惩罚无子者的法律、并弘扬宗教价值。
这一论证在世俗动机与异教皇帝（一方面）同宗教动机与基督教皇帝（另一方面）之间作出了强烈对比。
en: The distinction is sometimes made casually, because it was usually taken for granted. It did not require great conceptual leaps. To give some examples at random, Constantine distinguished between strife within the Church and in the “outside” world.
Photios says that the historian Sergios covered the events both of the
and of the
Writers also distinguished between different types of authority—secular and ecclesiastical—and their respective bearers; this was a distinction based in the law.

Sacred law, that is, the canons of the Church Councils, was theoretically distinct from imperial law, even when the emperors chose to ratify the former and so endow it with imperial authority; Leon VI calls them
and
Psellos regularly distinguished between political (πολιτικώτερα) and spiritual (πνευματικώτερα) ways of life.
In his

Theophylaktos of Ohrid (or his rhetorical persona) brands as “secular” (κοσμικὴν) and as “inspired by the rulers of this world” the laws of the ancient emperors that outlawed the making of eunuchs. Their goal was to increase the population of the
and have more soldiers. Constantine, by contrast, annulled laws that penalized the childless and promoted religious values.
The argument draws a strong contrast between secular motives and pagan emperors (on the one hand) and religious motives and Christian emperors (on the other).

zh: 神圣与世俗之间的区分始终随手可用，并按每位作者所作论证的不同而以不同方式被使用。关于两者恰当关系的辩论，尤其在国家与教会层面，通常只在它被质疑时才浮出水面。拜占庭对此有一种活跃的思想交流，因为每一个主张都是对他人观点或实践的隐含或明确挑战。
大马士革的约翰（Ioannes of Damascus）论证说，在“那些关乎我们日常事务的事上，例如税收”，应当服从皇帝，但在教义上则不然。
斯图狄奥斯的狄奥多罗斯（Theodoros the Stoudite）告诉利奥五世，只管“治理
和军队”，“但别管教会。”
还能从那些觉得自己在某次帝国干预中处于败方的教士那里引到更多这类声明。
en: The distinction between sacred and secular was always at hand and used in different ways depending on the argument that each author was making. The debate over the proper relation between the two, especially at the level of State and Church, generally rose to the surface only when it was being contested. There was a vigorous exchange of ideas about this in Byzantium, because every claim was an implicit or explicit challenge to someone else’s view or practice.
Ioannes of Damascus argued that emperors should be obeyed when it came to “those matters which pertain to our daily lives, for example taxes,” but not when it came to doctrine.
Theodoros the Stoudite told Leon V to keep for himself “the ordering of the
and the armies, but leave the Church alone.”
Many more such statements can be cited from clerics who felt they were on the losing side of some imperial intervention.

zh: 所以，虽然没有一条单一教义不可更改地固定神圣与世俗的确切界限，却有一场关于这个问题的持续辩论，这揭示它始终被视为一个问题。但这样一个问题之所以可能存在，只是因为两者之间的理论区分对整个文化是
；如果区分不存在——如许多历史学家所声称的那样——这个问题就不会存在。
此外，世俗生活的大多数方面根本不成问题。辩论主要关乎皇帝干预宗教生活某些方面的权利，而且只在特定情形下。皇帝在别处所做的大多数事，包括政治领域的大部分，被理解为世俗的，因此不成问题。（也有一场关于教士能在多大程度上参与某些国家活动、尤其是战争与死刑的辩论，这从另一侧划定了界限。）
en: So while there was no single doctrine immutably fixing the exact limits of the sacred and the secular, there was an ongoing debate about the issue, which reveals that it was always perceived as a problem. But such a problem could have existed only if the theoretical distinction between the two was
to the culture as a whole; the problem would not have existed if the distinction were nonexistent, as so many historians state.

Moreover, there was no issue at all about most aspects of secular life. The debate concerned largely the right of the emperor to intervene in certain aspects of religious life, and only under specific circumstances. Most of what the emperor did elsewhere, including most of the political sphere, was understood as secular and thus not problematic. (There was a debate also about the extent to which clergy could participate in certain state activities, especially war and capital punishment, and this drew boundaries from the other side.)

zh: 罗马人的政体始终带有宗教色彩，无论以异教还是基督教方式，但它不由宗教界定，更不由任何特定宗教界定。在其漫长历史中，罗马身份历经许多宗教发展、转变与皈依而存续。基督教会及其宗教模式起初是非罗马的，但最终变得对共和国不可或缺。尽管如此，它们从未构成它的总体。共和国是作为一个政治共同体、而非宗教共同体被构成的。它是世俗的，不是在这种意义上：它通过某种现代“分离”
宗教（那是一个转移视线的东西），而是在这种意义上：它不由宗教
。做一个东正教徒只是拜占庭共和国中做一个罗马人的一个方面，在大多数人心里也许是一个必要条件，却不是充分条件。事实上，就教会是一个“国家部门”、且大多服从帝国制度权威而言——其程度我们仍不理解——政体把它的宗教作为自身的一项属性和一种资源纳入进来。
我们在第1章看到，叙利亚诺斯（Syrianos，九世纪）如何把教士列入
的众多构成要素之中，与法律家、商人、士兵及其他人并列，他们各自以自己的方式促进共同善。
en: The polity of the Romans was always inflected religiously, whether in a pagan or Christian way, but it was not defined by religion, much less by any particular religion. During its long history, Roman identity survived through many religious developments, shifts, and conversions. The Christian Church and its religious modes started out as non-Roman but eventually became essential to the republic. Still, they never constituted its totality. The republic was constituted as a political and not a religious community. It was secular not in the sense that it
religion through some kind of modern “separation” (a red herring), but in that it was not

by it. Being Orthodox was only one aspect of being a Roman in the Byzantine republic, a necessary one perhaps in the minds of most but not a sufficient one. In fact, to the degree that the Church was a “department of state” and mostly subject to the authority of imperial institutions—to a degree that we still do not understand—the polity subsumed its religion as an attribute and property of itself.
We saw in Chapter 1 how Syrianos (in the ninth century) included priests among the many constituent elements of the
alongside lawyers, merchants, soldiers, and others, each of whom promoted the common good in his own way.

zh: 一些拜占庭人认为虔诚是其统治者更应具备的美德，另一些人则认为不那么重要。一些人选择把更多生命投入宗教，另一些人则较少。除了做基督徒还有别的事可做。想想佩特罗纳（Petronas），皇帝米海尔三世（Michael III）的舅父、他那个时代的一位领头将军。当他将死时，一位朋友恳请圣徒安东尼（Antonios）去探望他。但安东尼拒绝了，说：“这些世俗人守不住所许的诺言”（οἱ κοσμικοὶ πιστὰ οὐ φυλάσσουσι）。最终他去了，于是佩特罗纳对他说：“圣父，我要死了。”安东尼：“要死的不是一个基督徒。”佩特罗纳：“我承认我是基督徒，尽管我太清楚自己从未做过基督徒应做的事。”
许多、甚至大多数拜占庭人都能这么说，尽管他们的看法没有传世，不像圣徒与主教的看法那样。
en: Some Byzantines thought piety was a more important virtue for their rulers to have, others less. Some chose to devote more of their lives to religion, others less. There were other things to do than be Christian. Consider Petronas, the uncle of the emperor Michael III and a leading general of his age. When he was about to die, a friend begged the holy man Antonios to pay him a visit. But Antonios refused, saying, “These secular types don’t keep faith” (οἱ κοσμικοὶ πιστὰ οὐ φυλάσσουσι). Eventually he went, whereupon Petronas told him, “Holy father, I am dying.” Antonios: “It is not a Christian man who is dying.” Petronas: “I confess that I am a Christian, though I am all too aware that I have never done what Christians should do.”
The same could be said by many or even by most Byzantines, though their views have not survived, unlike the views of saints and bishops.

zh: 因此，在把拜占庭看作一种政治文化时，我同意雷·范·达姆最近所写的（正是关于君士坦丁），即我们能够且必须“抛弃对基督教的执念……那种一心只聚焦基督教的做法。”

我想以考察一些拜占庭关于帝国之力的世俗思考作结，它反驳保罗·亚历山大的否定论点。我推测，负责筹划帝国事务的人通常从世俗角度思考问题，但我们很少能瞥见他们的谋划。我们的史料大多反映后来作者的宗教偏见，那些作者被宗教机构选择保存下来。例如，现代历史学家一致认为，使拜占庭国家得以存续的因素之一是它高效的税收系统。一个庞大的装置被部署来运作它，但我们只有来自它的最寥寥的记录。这里我们再次撞上我们所知确曾如此之事与幸存史料所说之间的鸿沟。然而如果亚历山大是对的、拜占庭人不能以世俗方式思考，那他们如何运作这个财政系统？幸运的是我们不必猜测：皇帝们自己与许多其他作家都有记录在案。我上文引了查士丁尼论武器与法律的重要性。拜占庭人不仅能够以世俗方式思考他们国家的强项与失败，他们还经常把这些题目上的思考与本书所致力的拜占庭共和国构想联系起来。我将先聚焦他们的财政系统，然后转向拜占庭力量的其他世俗方面。
en: Therefore, in looking at Byzantium as a political culture, I agree with what Ray Van Dam has recently written (about Constantine no less), namely, that we can and must “discard the obsession with Christianity... the single-minded focus on Christianity.”

I would like to close with a survey of some Byzantine secular thinking regarding the strength of the empire, which refutes Paul Alexander’s negative thesis. I suspect that imperial planners thought in secular terms as a rule, but we can rarely glimpse their deliberations. Most of our sources reflect the religious bias of later authors whom religious institutions chose to preserve. For example, modern historians are unanimous that one of the factors that enabled the Byzantine state to survive was its efficient tax system. A vast apparatus was deployed to operate it, but we have only the barest records from it. Here again we run into the gap between what we know was the case and what surviving sources say. Yet if Alexander was right and the Byzantines could not think in secular terms, how did they operate this fiscal system? Fortunately we do not have to guess: the emperors themselves and many other writers are on record. I quoted Justinian on the importance of arms and laws above. Not only could the Byzantines think in secular terms about both the strength and failures of their state, they regularly linked their thoughts on these topics to the conception of the Byzantine republic to which this book has been devoted. I will focus first on their fiscal system, then move to other secular aspects of Byzantine strength.

zh: 人们充分理解国家需要钱来履行其基本职能。查士丁尼解释说，逃税威胁“我们
”的凝聚。
566年，其继任者查士丁二世指出，他继承的已经枯竭的帝国财源正在危及军队履行职责的能力。
巴西尔一世（Basileios I）即位时向元老院抱怨没有足够的钱支付公共开支。
阿莱克修斯一世（Alexios I）发现自己面对诺曼人入侵时没有钱、因此没有军队。
569年，查士丁二世曾详细解释税收如何运作，并在此过程中申明共和国的非人格性（注意加着重号的词句）：
en: It was well understood that the state needed money to carry out its basic functions. Justinian explained that tax evasion threatened the cohesion of “our
In 566 his successor Justin II noted that the bankrupt imperial finances he had inherited were jeopardizing the ability of the army to perform.
Basileios I complained to the senate upon his accession that there was not enough money to pay public obligations.
Alexios I found himself facing the Norman invasion with no money and so no army.
In 569 Justin II had explained at length how taxes worked, affirming, in the process, the impersonality of the republic (note the highlighted words):

zh: 这些规定不仅关乎总督；它们也适用于每一位官长的估税员与属吏，无论他是谁……我们唯一的目标是各行省能以良法治理、居民能在那里安居、享受总督所施正义的福祉，并且公共税收能无争议地征收；因为若不这样做，政府就不可能保全。正是由于士兵领到的军饷，他们才能抵抗敌人、保卫公民免受蛮族的入侵与残暴、保护田野与城镇免受盗匪及其他不法之徒的袭击。也正是通过税收，其他军团才领到应得的军饷，城墙才得以修缮、城市才得以设防、公共浴场才得以供暖，最后，供我们臣民消遣的剧场才得以维持。于是我们臣民缴纳的税被这样使用与花费，部分用于他们自身、部分间接为他们而花，

children: 因为我们从中不获取任何利益，只受托管理它们；

zh: 尽管如此，我们的辛劳已得到充分报偿，因为我们的主、我们的救主耶稣基督以其大慈大悲，赐给我们无尽的福祉。
en: These provisions relate not only to governors; they also apply to the assessors and officials of every magistrate, no matter who he may be... our only aim is that the provinces may be governed by good laws and that persons may reside there in safety and enjoy the blessings of justice as dispensed by the governors, and that the public taxes may be collected without controversy; for when this is not done, it will be impossible for the government to be preserved. It is because of the pay received by them that soldiers are enabled to resist the enemy and defend citizens from the invasions and cruelty of the barbarians, and protect fields and towns from the attacks of robbers and others living a disorderly life. It is also by means of taxation that the other cohorts receive what is allotted to them, that walls are repaired, cities fortified, public baths warmed, and, finally, the theatres intended for the diversion of our subjects supported. Thus the taxes paid by our subjects are used and expended, partly for themselves, and partly indirectly on their account,

children: for we do not derive any benefit from them, and are only charged with their administration;

en: still, we are fully rewarded for our trouble by the infinite blessings which our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ has bestowed upon us through the greatness of his clemency.

zh: 这并未显示出对帝国基础的理解弱于塔西佗笔下克里亚利斯（Cerialis）那句著名而常被引用的声明，即没有士兵就没有和平；没有军饷就没有士兵；没有税收就没有军饷。
这似乎是罗马治理的一条历代相传的治理箴言。
en: This does not reveal a weaker understanding of the basis of empire than the famous and often-quoted statement by Cerialis in Tacitus, namely, that you cannot have peace without soldiers; or soldiers without pay; or pay without taxation.
This seems to have been a diachronic maxim of Roman governance.

zh: 利奥六世（九世纪晚期）告诫他的将军们“要关心农民。我认为这两种营生对于一个民族（
）的构成与存续真正至关重要：农耕滋养并强化士兵，而军队为农民讨还公道，并保护他们。其他生活营生在我看来次于这两者”（但在同一文本稍后不同的修辞语境中，他把宗教与教士放在“高于一切”的位置）。
在其关于军役土地的立法中，利奥之子君士坦丁七世（Konstantinos VII）开篇声明“正如头之于身体，军队之于
亦然……谁若不把这些事置于极大的关切（
）之下，谁就在自身安全上犯错，尤其是当他把共同利益（
）视为他自己的安全领域时。”
甚至人口论证也有佐证。在他934年那部禁止“强势者”获取村社土地的重要《新律》（
）中，罗曼努斯一世（Romanos I）认识到人口与人口结构一方面同税收与军队另一方面之间的关联：
en: Leon VI (late ninth century) advised his generals to “be concerned about the farmers. I think that these two pursuits are truly essential for the constitution and permanence of a nation

farming nourishes and strengthens the soldiers, whereas the military avenges and protects the farmers. The other life-pursuits impress me as second to these” (but in different rhetorical context later in the same text, he puts religion and the priests “above everything else”).
In his legislation regarding the military lands, Leon’s son Konstantinos VII began by stating that “as the head is to the body, so is the army to the
... He who does not subject these matters to great care
errs with respect to his own safety, especially if he regards the common interest
as his own realm of security.”
Even demographic arguments are attested. In his great
of 934 barring the “powerful” from acquiring lands in village communes, Romanos I recognized the link between population and demography on the one hand and taxes and the military on the other:

zh: 因为人口聚居地彰显了其功能的巨大益处——缴纳税款、承担兵役——一旦平民消失，这些将完全丧失。关心国家稳定的人必须消除动乱的根源、驱逐有害之物、并支持共同善（
en: For population settlements demonstrate the great benefit of their function—the contribution of taxes and the fulfillment of military obligations—which will be completely lost should the common people disappear. Those concerned with the stability of the state must eliminate the cause of disturbance, expel what is harmful, and support the common good

zh: 其他作家也解释了帝国治理系统如何运作。叙利亚诺斯（九世纪）在其对共和国各贡献阶层的综述中，解释了国家财政系统的功能：
en: Other writers also explained how imperial systems of governance worked. In his survey of the different classes contributing to the republic, Syrianos (ninth century) explains the function of the state fiscal system:

zh: 财政系统（τὸ χρηματικὸν）的设立是为了照管不时出现的公共重要事务，例如建造船只与城墙。但它主要关乎发放军饷。每年大部分公共收入都花在这一目的上。
en: The fiscal system (τὸ χρηματικὸν) was set up to take care of matters of public importance that arise on occasion, such as the building of ships and walls. But it is principally concerned with paying the soldiers. Each year most of the public revenues are spent for this purpose.

zh: 他接着具体说明财政官员必须具备的技能：
en: He then specifies the skills that fiscal officials must have:

zh: 他们必须懂一些测量、农业方法与会计。因为为征税而估定的数额基于土地面积、也基于其质量、及其作物产出或金属资源。他们必须能够估计气候、地形〔等等〕的影响。
en: They must have some knowledge of surveying, of agricultural methods, and of accounting. For the amounts assessed for tax purposes are based upon the area of land, and upon its quality as well, and its productivity in crops or resources in metal. They must be able to estimate the effects of climate, topography [and so on].

zh: 约翰·哈尔登写道，“拜占庭军队被视为国家装置的一个独特分支，由皇帝的臣民组成，由国家通过其税收装备与供养，被招募与付饷以执行一组特定而有限的任务。”
en: John Haldon has written that “the Byzantine army was perceived as a distinct branch of the state apparatus, composed of subjects of the emperor, equipped and supported by the state through its taxes, recruited and paid to carry out a specific and limited set of tasks.”

zh: 诚然，始终有可能主张“真正”要紧的是祈祷而非金钱、军队或联盟，而我们看到连查士丁尼都准备这么说。
更正确的说法毋宁是：存在一些修辞时刻，其中某些人偶尔运用这类论证。不清楚是否有人曾“相信”它们或把它们付诸实践；此外，它们会很难评估，因为没有人认真准备检验一种“只靠祈祷”的策略。当君士坦丁九世决定不要卫士、只信靠上帝时，普塞洛斯试图让他明白事理，说船长、建筑师与将军也信靠上帝，却也实施与其技艺相关的务实措施。
en: To be sure, it was always possible to argue that what “really” counted was prayer and not money, armies, or alliances, and we saw that even Justinian was prepared to say that.

It is more correct to say, rather, that there were rhetorical moments in which some people occasionally deployed such arguments. It is not clear that anyone ever “believed” them or put them into practice; besides, they would have been difficult to evaluate as no one was seriously prepared to test a “prayer only” strategy. When Konstantinos IX decided to dispense with guards and trust only in God, Psellos tried to talk sense into him by saying that ship captains, architects, and generals also trust in God but implement practical measures relating to their art.

zh: 普塞洛斯对帝国的运作持一种世俗观点，并为我们提供了它十一世纪衰落的一种世俗解释。君士坦丁九世未能认识到支撑罗马权力的有两样东西：其官职系统与金钱，再加一样：对它们的明智督察与理性分配。
太多皇帝以为只要争取到文官的支持，皇位就稳固了，但事实上他们需要赢得并保持都城民众、元老院与军队的欢心。
（如我们所见，普塞洛斯在这一点上完全正确。）当伊萨克·科穆宁（Isaakios Komnenos）决定在小亚细亚叛乱时，他明智地切断与都城的通讯、并挪用税收收入以支付其军队、奖赏其支持者，但他也确保税册保持更新，以免日后有人有怨望。
最后，在其《编年史》（
）原始版本的结尾，普塞洛斯停下来回顾过去三十年（1025–1057），解释“共和国的身体”（τὸ τῆς πολιτείας σῶμα）出了什么问题。他就政府系统的管理不善提出了一个敏锐的论证，聚焦财政浪费、领薪头衔的激增、以及对军队的忽视。
这是一种完全世俗的分析；普塞洛斯不仅不把神义论带进来，还一贯批评皇帝把钱花在修道院之类上。
en: Psellos had a secular view of the workings of the empire and offers us a secular explanation for its decline during the eleventh century. Konstantinos IX failed to realize that two things support Roman power, its system of offices and money, plus one more: their intelligent oversight and rational distribution.
Too many emperors thought that they were safe so long as they won over the civil officials, but in fact they needed to gain and keep the favor of the populace of the City, the senate, and the armies.

(As we have seen, Psellos was entirely correct about this.) When Isaakios Komnenos decided to rebel in Asia Minor, he wisely cut communications to the capital and appropriated the tax revenues in order to pay his army and reward his supporters, but he also made sure that tax registers were kept up to date so that no one would have grievances later.
Finally, at the end of the original version of his

Psellos pauses to look back over the past thirty years (1025–1057) and explain what went wrong with “the body of the republic” (τὸ τῆς πολιτείας σῶμα). He offers an astute argument about the mismanagement of the system of government, focusing on fiscal waste, the multiplication of salaried titles, and the neglect of the armies.
It is an entirely secular analysis; not only does Psellos not bring theodicy into it, he consistently criticizes emperors for spending money on monasteries and the like.

zh: 同一衰落时期也被普塞洛斯的同时代人与熟人阿塔莱亚特斯（Attaleiates）分析过。他的《历史》（
）同样强调不合理的施政如何带来失败，并把罗马人的苦难不是归于上帝的愤怒，而是归于他们自己腐朽的政治文化。
他明确说异端与这类神学罪行与此无关：过错全在罗马的统治者施政无方。
例如，君士坦丁十世（Konstantinos X）对军队关注太少，结果外省人在看到税收上涨的同时暴露于敌人入侵。
尼基弗鲁斯·布里恩尼奥斯（Nikephoros Bryennios）对尼基弗鲁斯三世·博塔内亚特斯失败的批评，同样围绕博塔内亚特斯糟糕的财政政策。
en: The same period of decline was analyzed by Psellos’s contemporary and acquaintance Attaleiates. His
likewise stressed the theme of irrational mismanagement and blamed the Romans’ woes not on God’s anger but on their own rotten political culture.
He was explicit that heresy and such theological crimes had nothing to do with it: it was all the fault of bad Roman leadership.
For example, Konstantinos X paid too little attention to the armies, with the result that provincials were exposed to enemy invasions just as they were seeing their taxes rise.
Nikephoros Bryennios’s critique of the failures of Nikephoros III Botaneiates likewise revolved around Botaneiates’s bad fiscal policies.

zh: 虽然它们只是一个样本，上文呈现的段落与作者表明，拜占庭人能够以与现代历史学家大致相同的方式解释他们帝国的强项与失败。正如在联系西方中世纪研究时已被指出的，“[现代]中世纪政治思想史家所呈现的意识形态，有时似乎不仅与中世纪政治史家所描述的现实脱节，也与大多数参与中世纪治理者的观念脱节。”
en: Though they are but a sample, the passages and authors presented above demonstrate that the Byzantines could explain the strengths and failures of their empire in more or less the same ways as modern historians. As has been noted in connection with western Medieval Studies, “the ideology presented by [modern] historians of medieval political ideas has sometimes seemed divorced not only from the realities described by historians of medieval politics but from the ideas of most of those involved in medieval government.”

zh: 许多拜占庭历史学家与其他作家也把皇帝不是当作上帝的受膏者，而是当作公共资源的管理者与管家。
这不是因为他们的精英教育使他们更老练。本书已表明，活跃的辩论与动态的交流在拜占庭政治领域的所有层面、所有时候都是其特征。君士坦丁堡与其他主要城市的平民，同样能够轻易地从赞美皇帝为上帝受膏者，切换到抗议其财政或宗教政策、并用性的言辞辱骂他。佛提乌在其致保加利亚国王鲍里斯（Boris）的劝诫信中说，那些治理者“即便他们一个小小的失误也会被放大、被每个人到处谈论，于是闹得人尽皆知。”
普塞洛斯扩展了这一观念，解释说这是因为拜占庭公共辩论的尖刻性质：即便你想做好事，也总会有人把你的善意说歪。皇帝们似乎捞不到任何喘息。
我们又回到谢内（Cheynet）所揭示的“舆论的多变与皇权的脆弱”。
没有皇帝能用足够多的上帝话语把自己裹起来、以求免受共和国的凶险，而即便一个正派人也可能被认为不足以胜任该职位的管理任务。
人们理解皇帝只是有恶习与缺陷的凡人。也许一位皇帝对另一位皇帝说过的最悲观的话是：“许多皇帝曾住在这座宫殿里，但很少曾住在天国里。”
en: Many Byzantine historians and other authors too treated the emperor not as God’s anointed but as a manager and steward of public resources.

This was not because their elite education made them more sophisticated. This book has demonstrated that vigorous debate and dynamic exchanges characterized the political sphere of Byzantium on all levels and at all times. The common people of Constantinople and other major cities could just as easily switch from praising the emperor as God’s anointed to protesting against his financial or religious policies, and to insulting him sexually. In his letter of advice to Boris, the king of Bulgaria, Photios says of those who govern that “even a small mistake of theirs is inflated, talked about everywhere by everyone, and so it becomes notorious.”

Psellos expanded on this idea, explaining that this was because of the acerbic nature of public debate in Byzantium: even if you tried to do good, people would be found to twist it around. Emperors, it seems, could not catch any breaks.
We are back to what Cheynet exposed as “the versatility of public opinion and the fragility of imperial power.”
No emperor could wrap himself in enough God-talk to feel safe from the perils of the republic, and even a decent man could be regarded as inadequate to the managerial tasks of the office.

It was understood that emperors were only mortal men with vices and flaws. Probably the most pessimistic thing said by one emperor to another was that “many emperors have lived in this palace, but few have lived in the kingdom of heaven.”

zh: 归根结底，帝国理念不过是那套把共和国维系在一起、确保其活力的角色、权利与责任的复杂系统中的一种模态。我们应当停止把它用作我们的阿基米德点，因为拜占庭人自己并不这样做。即便当他们说自己这样做时。
en: In the end, the imperial idea was but one modality in the complex system of roles, rights, and responsibilities that held the republic together and ensured its vitality. We should stop using it as our Archimedean point, for the Byzantines themselves did not. Even when they said they did.

zh: 即使后世认定为正统的皇帝被一个“异端”取代，情况也是如此：前者才是“僭主”，即不具正当性的篡位者。正统皇帝落败了，因此他没有得到上帝的眷顾，哪怕从宗教立场出发他本该蒙受眷顾。阿尔塔巴斯多斯一例见 Koutrakou,
297，另见281。有人主张，帝国理念确实影响了这一政体，但影响是负面的。它助长了内战，因为击败在位皇帝而夺得帝位意味着你才是蒙上帝眷顾的人。这一理念也使拜占庭人尤其容易在帝国遭蛮族击败时起而反对自己的皇帝，因为他们认为这些皇帝已失去上帝的眷顾，而那恰恰是最不该这样做的时候。见 Treadgold, “Byzantium, the Reluctant Warrior,” 228。
en: This was even the case when an emperor viewed in retrospect as orthodox was replaced by a “heretic”: it was the former who was the “tyrant,” i.e., the illegitimate usurper. The orthodox emperor had lost; therefore he had not been favored by God, even if on religious grounds he should have been. See Koutrakou,

297, for the case of Artabasdos; also 281. A case has been made that the imperial idea did have an impact on the polity, but a negative one, namely, that it encouraged civil wars (because gaining the throne against a sitting emperor meant that you were God’s favorite), and also that it made the Byzantines attack their emperors especially when the empire was being defeated by barbarians, i.e., at the worst possible time, because those emperors were perceived as having lost God’s favor: Treadgold, “Byzantium, the Reluctant Warrior,” 228.

zh: 现代术语“皇帝教皇主义”构成一道障碍，因为在近现代信奉天主教和新教的西方，这种安排被视作坏事。历史学家急于按照西方的标准为拜占庭“恢复名誉”，于是拒绝将它用于拜占庭，也因此无法解释皇帝相对于教会所处的位置。这个僵局出自如下逻辑：如果西方学者认为某件事很坏，那就不可能发生在拜占庭，因为我们现在要证明拜占庭并没有那么坏。可是，天主教和新教思想家认为什么样的政教关系才合宜，我们为何要在意？拜占庭人身为罗马人，对这个问题自有看法。
en: An obstacle is posed by the modern term “Caesaropapism,” deemed a bad thing in the modern Catholic-Protestant West. In their rush to “rehabilitate” Byzantium on western terms, historians have rejected its applicability and have thereby made themselves unable to explain the emperor’s position vis-à-vis the Church. The impasse results from the following logic: if western scholars think it’s bad, then it can’t have been true of Byzantium, which we now want to show was not bad. But why should we care what Catholic-Protestant thinkers believe is right for Church-State relations? The Byzantines, being Romans, had their own ideas about this.
